items.album: NYC’s Some Days Are Darker Explore the Anatomy of Obsession in Video for “Memorize You”
items.excerpt: Love songs usually get nervous around obsession because nobody wants to admit how close the two can live together. Everybody likes devotion when it comes with flowers, candy, and clean shirts. Start remembering somebody’s freckles individually, and suddenly the room gets quieter. New York’s Some Days Are Darker explores that uneasy proximity on Memorize You, a song with the posture of romance and the blood pressure of somebody who has been awake far too long thinking about one person. Lear Mason
items.body: Love songs usually get nervous around obsession because nobody wants to admit how close the two can live together. Everybody likes devotion when it comes with flowers, candy, and clean shirts. Start remembering somebody’s freckles individually, and suddenly the room gets quieter. New York’s Some Days Are Darker explores that uneasy proximity on Memorize You, a song with the posture of romance and the blood pressure of somebody who has been awake far too long thinking about one person. Lear Mason sings, “I want to memorize you, your freckles and scars, the longing in your eyes, the rhythm of your heart,” and the sweetness of the line grows more complicated with each detail. There is love in there, certainly, but there is also the ancient human urge to pin beauty to the wall before it can leave. A thick, metallic bassline gives Memorize You its physical weight, while the drums tighten the tension and chiming synth melodies introduce a nervous sweetness. Mason’s croon carries the seductive assurance of early ’90s alternative rock, making even the most exposed confession sound as though it has been rehearsed for one particular listener. Around him, Chris Martin and Robbie Williamson build pressure through the interplay of bass, drums, guitars, and keyboards, gradually filling the space his voice initially leaves open. The arrangement gives the song’s gothic romanticism a muscular foundation, allowing its tenderness and possessiveness to press uncomfortably close together. What begins as an intimate confession grows into a feverish rush, increasingly expansive and overwhelming, until desire and desperation become difficult to separate. The largely black-and-white video gives this fixation a distinctly New York setting, following a woman through Washington Square Park and beneath its familiar marble arch. Daylight smiles and close-ups alternate with nighttime walks past illuminated storefronts, parked cars, and iron railings, while Mason sings to the camera in a tightly framed interior. The repeated attention to her face makes a visual counterpart to the lyrics, collecting expressions as though enough looking might finally amount to knowing someone. But a masked figure brings a more literal threat into view, and her glances over her shoulder become increasingly uneasy. That unease develops into a pursuit through the streets and into narrow basement corridors, where exposed pipes and bare walls replace the park’s open space. The closing switch to colour brings pursuer and pursued face to face: two women whose similar hair and red lipstick give the encounter the unsettling suggestion of a double. It is a fitting complication for a song so concerned with committing another person to memory, leaving the desire to recognize someone tangled up with the fear of what recognition might reveal. Watch the video for Memorize You below: Mason began Some Days Are Darker in 2019 as a solitary songwriting project after years playing metalcore guitar. It has since become a three-piece built around his chemistry with bassist, guitarist, and keyboardist Chris Martin and drummer, multi-instrumentalist, and producer Robbie Williamson. Between them, the musicians bring decades of experience to songs that draw on gothic grandeur, synth-driven alternative rock, and the charged intimacy of noir cinema. Their self-titled 2022 debut introduced a musical world in which longing can become obsession and physical closeness offers no guarantee against feeling alone. That combination has found a home on stages alongside The Chameleons, Vision Video, and House of Harm, with the trio also touring the US East Coast and Canada with Pink Turns Blue and the US West Coast with Theatre of Hate. Further East Coast dates are planned around the November release of their forthcoming album, Black Box Warning. Recorded with Dave Catching at Rancho de la Luna in Joshua Tree, California, Black Box Warning expands these concerns across twelve songs about desire and its consequences, making room for love, loss, lust, and the possibility of beginning again. The desert studio, whose visitors have included Iggy Pop, Queens of the Stone Age, and PJ Harvey, provides the setting for some of the band’s most intense and expansive material alongside its most exposed performances. A solo acoustic piece and a closing piano ballad extend the album’s emotional range, bringing the same difficult questions into quieter rooms. For Some Days Are Darker, the attraction lies in that uncertainty: whether giving yourself over to someone will bring you closer to life or further from yourself. Memorize You makes the surrender sound seductive enough to postpone the question. Learning someone by heart is a beautiful ambition; expecting the heart to survive the exercise unaltered is another matter. items.body: alarm!systemen self-titled Antibody Belgian newcomer alarm!systemen’s debut LP has a range of sounds and approaches which often belies a lack of direction or aesthetic, but that’s definitely not the case here. At large, the ten tracks on offer draw from long histories of coldwave and dream pop, but eschew slavish adherence to lo-fi nostalgia for its own sake. The classic Slowdive-isms of “Goes Again” are offset by clean, if minimal modern programming, and later on album closer “Void” serves as a reminder of how that act and other shoegaze giants found new life lifting from ambient electronics at large. On the more direct side, “Kapot” juxtaposes bricked-out synthpop drum programming with excellently reverbed guitar, and the dead simple but wonderfully executed dream pop nod of “BURN” shows just how far some wistful melodies and airy production can take you when they’re done with a measure of taste and restraint. Written over the course of five years, it’s perhaps not surprising that there’s this much variety here, but alarm!systemen’s real forte is in pulling it all off well enough to refresh familiar styles and serve as an example of how younger acts drawn to these classic sounds can rework and rethink them in their own manner. alarm!systemen by alarm!systemen Zataar First Crush CRVSH While based in France, the material released by producer Zataar draws from both her Morrocan and Belgian heritage. From the latter, you funky rhythmic electronics that hearken back to the New Beat era with a healthy dose of classic body music, where the former comes through in the melodies and instrumentation that reference North African folk music. Cuts like “Ali Sawtek” lean into the blend especially well, finding a swinging groove in the bass and drum programming, while Zataar’s vocals and the track’s melody are kept low and swirling in the mix, with big string stabs cutting through the thick reverb. As a contrast, “In the Lights You Call My Name” injects polyrhythmic complexity into the drum track, its belchy resonant bassline flowing beneath rich waves of plucks and pads. The cleverness in the arrangements really comes through on “Moments in Love”, which manages transitions between deep house styled rhythm programming and sections of Chaabi folk melodies, before combining them smoothly into a hypnotic whole. Far from a gimmick, it’s a fully realized approach that recognizes the commonality and contrasts inherent in blending multiple styles and genres, and then reconciles them handily. items.body:
25 editions in, Baybeats 2026 proved that there is still plenty of room for discovery at Singapore's longest-running alternative music festival. Across 3 – 6 September, 48 acts filled Esplanade with everything from crushing experimental rock and abrasive post-punk to homegrown hip-hop and Thai roots reggae. It was diverse, unpredictable and, most importantly, a whole lot of fun. Here are five sets that stayed with us.

Boris

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by borisheavyrocks (@borisdronevil)

Few bands can make sheer volume feel as nuanced as Boris. The Japanese experimental rock veterans shifted through sludge, drone, noise, psychedelia and shoegaze with an almost elemental force, building enormous walls of sound before pulling them back into quieter, more hypnotic passages. Heavy without ever becoming one-dimensional, their set was a masterclass in how distortion, dynamics and atmosphere can work together to completely swallow a room.

DAVID BORING

Credit: danspixelgraphy, courtesy of Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay

There was something almost hypnotic about DAVID BORING, even at their most confrontational. The Hong Kong outfit constantly alternated between danceable, propulsive grooves and sudden bursts of abrasive post-punk noise, creating a tension between release and unease that kept the room locked in. That push and pull between raw dissonance and meticulous control became considerably more visceral onstage. Chaotic without feeling careless, this was a set that made it difficult to look away.

Kin Leonn x pureblue Ensemble

Credit: chrawme, courtesy of Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay

Kin Leonn x pureblue Ensemble took the collective's already intricate, ambient and contemporary compositions and gave them new depth. Joined by Bryan de Rozario on saxophone, Lucas Tee on drums and Mervin Wong on viola, the ensemble added breath, movement and physicality to music built on delicacy and restraint. Combined with the breathtaking visuals, every small detail seemed more textured and visceral, turning the performance into an incredibly immersive audiovisual experience. The result was a set that felt expansive, tactile, and completely absorbing.

Mediocre Haircut Crew

Credit: alvieisalive, courtesy of Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay

Mediocre Haircut Crew's return to Baybeats felt less like a comeback set and more like a block party with a few hundred friends. Backed by a full live band led by music director Kenzo Nagari, omarKENOBI, mickeyLEANO and daniKIDDO sounded bigger without losing the easy chemistry, impeccable live flow and stage charisma that have always made them such a fun act to watch. They debuted new material alongside favourites including 'Lose Your Love' and 'Fuck Da System', before ending with a full-crowd sing-along to 'WANNABES'. If there was any rust to shake off, you certainly couldn't hear it.

Srirajah Rockers

Credit: won997, courtesy of Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay

Srirajah Rockers brought a completely different kind of vibe to Baybeats — one driven by groove rather than sheer volume. The Thai veterans' blend of roots reggae, heavy dub, Thai soul, lovers rock, ska and funk unfolded with an easy confidence, leaving plenty of space for deep bass and laid-back rhythms to breathe. Warm, hypnotic and effortlessly danceable, the set showed why more than two decades together have made the group such an enduring presence in Thailand's reggae scene. Amid a weekend of wide-ranging sounds, Srirajah Rockers stood out by locking into an irresistible groove.

Like what you read? Show our writer some love!

items.body: For all its stunning virtuosity, the tumbling fingerstyle guitar of Swedish guitarist Finn Loxbo is always in service to a set of brilliant compositional ideas Digging through the various improvised solo and duo recordings Swedish guitarist Finn Loxbo has made over the last decade is like witnessing a slow-motion creative winnowing, observing how a feverish pile of ideas and experiments has gradually coalesced into something inscrutable. His third solo album Lummernikt is a work of astonishing focus and originality forged from familiar notions, a free improvisation practice patiently chiseled into compositional rigour. Across eight riveting acoustic pieces played live without overdubs, Loxbo melds extended technique, fingerstyle fluency and self-devised preparations to deliver one of the year’s most beguiling, detailed and beautiful... items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是瑞典吉他手Finn Loxbo的第三张个人作品，汇集了他过去十年即兴独奏与二重奏录音中沉淀下来的创作精华。整张专辑由八首原声吉他作品组成，现场录制无后期叠加，体现了演奏的纯粹性。Loxbo将扩展技法、指弹的流畅性以及自制的吉他准备器结合在一起，把自由即兴的实践逐步雕刻成具有作曲严谨性的作品。他的技术服务于作曲理念而非炫技本身，作品中展现出惊人的专注力与原创性，从熟悉的素材中锻造出独特的音乐语言。评论强调这张专辑是近年来最具魅力、细节丰富且美的作品之一，融合了即兴精神与结构化的作曲思维，适合对原声吉他实验音乐感兴趣的听众。

items.body: Review by ElenaNL — The music is simply amazing. This album feels quite different from the other music by Compassionizer. As I listened to the tracks, I felt as if I were taking a journey around the world?and then even farther, into the Universe.There are subtle folk motifs that seem to echo Slavic heritage, intertwined with oriental influences and sounds that somehow touch the rhythm of the heartbeat. The combination creates a feeling of movement, discovery, and something almost timeless.I'm a dreamer by nature, and I love to "travel" through time, imagine distant places, and create worlds that don't exist anywhere except in my imagination. The music on this album feels like a perfect companion for that kind of journey. It doesn't simply fill the background?it guides the dreams, opens space for deep thoughts, and gives the imagination somewhere to wander.The vocals are a beautiful addition to the overall experience. They add another layer to the music without taking away from its atmospheric and almost cinematic quality.What I especially appreciate is the feeling the album leaves behind. It doesn't feel heavy or overwhelming, and there is no unpleasant aftertaste or excessive excitement. Instead, it leaves me with a sense of freshness, as if my mind has been gently cleared and filled with new thoughts.Each track feels like a small story of its own, with its own characters, atmosphere, journey, and ending. Together, the tracks create something that feels like a collection of little worlds?each one inviting you to step inside for a while and see where it takes you.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑呈现出一次跨越地理与时空的声音旅行，将斯拉夫民间母题与东方元素交织，辅以贴近心跳律动的节奏纹理，构建出兼具运动感与发现感的氛围体验。人声作为附加层次融入，不破坏整体的电影化氛围感。专辑没有沉重感或过度亢奋的刺激，听后留下清新的余韵，仿佛思绪被轻轻清理并注入新的想法。每一首曲目都像是独立的小故事，拥有各自的角色、氛围与旅程轨迹，合在一起则构成一个可逐一踏入探索的小世界集合。整体制作偏向氛围与叙事，适合作为引导沉思与想象的背景基底。

The track is the third single from Ignea’s upcoming album “Monumental,” due October 23, 2026 via Napalm Records, and pairs Ignea vocalist Helle Bohdanova with LaPlegua on an industrial metal cut built around aggrotech and electro-industrial textures. “Prefab” looks at architecture and collective memory, themes that run through “Monumental,” which
items.body: Ukrainian modern metal band Ignea have released a new single, Prefab, featuring Andy LaPlegua of Combichrist. The track is the third single from Ignea’s upcoming album “Monumental,” due October 23, 2026 via Napalm Records, and pairs Ignea vocalist Helle Bohdanova with LaPlegua on an industrial metal cut built around aggrotech and electro-industrial textures. “Prefab” looks at architecture and collective memory, themes that run through “Monumental,” which the band describes as centered on nostalgia. Bohdanova wrote the lyrics; the music was composed by keyboardist Yevhenii Zhytniuk with additional contributions from Bohdanova. Bohdanova commented on the track: “‘Prefab’ reflects on the darker side of nostalgia – prefabricated socialist buildings, originally meant to give everyone a roof over their heads. But like many socialist ideals, the concept was flawed at its core: uniform, industrial, stripping people of individuality and personal choice, making them feel like ants inside their own homes. Remnants of this architecture still stand across Europe – from Ukraine and Poland, from Germany to France. As Ukrainians from a post-Soviet country, we grew up surrounded by the physical remains of a system that promised a bright future and delivered the opposite. In the ‘Prefab’ video, we wanted to convey the feeling of a confined, uniform space, a cramped room representing a typical Soviet apartment, where only the tenants ever change. When we shaped the demo, we were basically hearing Andy’s vocals in the back of our minds, and we’re so glad he agreed to lend his voice. Having Combichrist as part of the industrial metal track on our upcoming album […]” Andy LaPlegua formed Combichrist in 2003 as a solo studio project, building it into one of the touchstone acts of the aggrotech and industrial metal scenes alongside his other projects Icon of Coil and Panzer AG. Combichrist’s most recent album, “The Venom In The Mouth Of God,” was announced via Out Of Line Music earlier in 2026, following singles including “Demons Wanna Be Summoned” with King 810 and “Feraline.” “Monumental” is Ignea’s second full-length album, following 2023’s “Dreams of Lands Unseen.” Writing and recording took place largely during the winter of 2025-2026, amid icy temperatures and long power outages in Kyiv during the full-scale war in Ukraine. Bohdanova described the record’s concept: “Back in the 17th century, nostalgia was considered a deadly disease – and in many ways, it still is. Much of this album was inspired by modernist architecture – concrete giants built to signal progress and a brighter future, now slowly decaying.” The album spans nine tracks: “Darkness,” “Dreams of Lands Unseen,” “Presence of the Past,” “Prefab” (feat. Combichrist), “What Buildings Dream of,” “I am in Hell,” “Between No Longer and Not Yet,” “Harmony Manufactured” (feat. Hiraes), and “Nadir.” Mixing and mastering were handled by Grammy-nominated producer Jacob Hansen, whose credits include Delain, Amaranthe, Volbeat, Amon Amarth, Arch Enemy and Epica. “Monumental” arrives on translucent dark night blue splatter vinyl with booklet, solid silver vinyl, CD jewelcase, a CD/T-shirt bundle, and digitally, released via Napalm Records. Ignea will support Evergrey’s “Architects Of A New Weave” European tour alongside Stellar Circuits starting in November, taking “Prefab” and the rest of “Monumental” to stages across Scandinavia, the UK and mainland Europe. Ignea tour dates 11 November 2026 – Lund, Sweden – Mejeriet 12 November 2026 – Stockholm, Sweden – Kollektivet Livet 13 November 2026 – Linkoping, Sweden – Paletset 14 November 2026 – Gothenburg, Sweden – Filmstudion 2 15 November 2026 – Oslo, Norway – Salt 17 November 2026 – Hamburg, Germany – Logo 18 November 2026 – Berlin, Germany – Hole44 19 November 2026 – Munich, Germany – Feierwerk 20 November 2026 – Vienna, Austria – Weberknecht 21 November 2026 – Milan, Italy – Slaughter Club 22 November 2026 – Aarau, Switzerland – KiFF 23 November 2026 – Antwerp, Belgium – Zappa 25 November 2026 – Southampton, UK – The Brook 26 November 2026 – Birmingham, UK – Asylum 27 November 2026 – London, UK – The Underworld 28 November 2026 – Leeds, UK – The Key Club 29 November 2026 – Dublin, Ireland – Opium 30 November 2026 – Belfast, UK – Limelight 2 1 December 2026 – Glasgow, UK – G2 2 December 2026 – Newcastle, UK – Anarchy Brew 3 December 2026 – Manchester, UK – Rebellion 4 December 2026 – Bristol, UK – Strange Brew 5 December 2026 – Nottingham, UK – Saltbox 7 December 2026 – Paris, France – Petit Bain 8 December 2026 – Trier, Germany – Mergener Hof 9 December 2026 – Karlsruhe, Germany – Substage 10 December 2026 – Dortmund, Germany – Junkyard 11 December 2026 – Rotterdam, Netherlands – Baroeg 12 December 2026 – Maastricht, Netherlands – Muziekgieterij About Ignea Ignea formed in Ukraine in 2013, releasing the EP “Sputnik” the same year. The band mixes melodic and progressive metal with symphonic, electronic and folk elements, building material around narrative concepts. Ignea’s debut full-length, “The Sign of Faith,” followed in 2017. The band’s early single “Alga,” released as a hymn referencing the Crimean Tatars’ battle cry after the annexation of Crimea, became the first original song by a Ukrainian metal band recorded with a full symphonic orchestra. Ignea’s second album, “The Realms of Fire and Death” (2020), was funded through the band’s Patreon page and was later named Ukraine’s metal album of the year. A split EP with Ersedu, “BESTIA,” followed in 2021. After building an independent following through two albums and two EPs, Ignea signed to Napalm Records and released “Dreams of Lands Unseen” in 2023, an album dedicated to Ukrainian travel writer and photographer Sofia Yablonska. Despite the ongoing war, the band toured extensively, including a 43-date EU/UK run supporting Fear Factory, and has since played festivals including Wacken Open Air, Summer Breeze, Bloodstock and Brutal Assault, alongside club dates with Cradle of Filth, Epica and Butcher Babies. Nine Ignea tracks also feature in the video game “S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl.” The current lineup is Helle Bohdanova (vocals), Yevhenii Zhytniuk (keyboards), Dmytro Vinnichenko (guitars) and Oleksandr Kamyshyn (bass). Ignea’s second full-length, “Monumental,” follows “Dreams of Lands Unseen” on October 23, 2026, led by the singles “Prefab” featuring Andy LaPlegua and its predecessors, and supported by the band’s November-December European tour with Evergrey.

items._cn_summary: 乌克兰现代金属乐队Ignea发布新单曲《Prefab》，与Combichrist主唱Andy LaPlegua合作。曲目融合工业金属与聚合科技、电子工业质感，由乐队键盘手Yevhenii Zhytniuk作曲，主唱Helle Bohdanova填词并参与编曲。歌词聚焦于预制板式社会主义建筑所承载的集体记忆——那些承诺平等却剥夺个性的灰色公寓，以及现代主义混凝土巨构在理想破灭后的缓慢衰败。整张专辑《Monumental》录制于2025至2026年冬天的基辅，正值全面战争期间频繁停电与严寒之中，将怀旧视为一种延续至今的致命病症。专辑共九首曲目，延续了前作《Dreams of Lands Unseen》的方向，由Napam Records发行。

items.body: Laho is a Finnish project that originated in 2006. After releasing a few records during its early years, the project went quiet for a long time before being reactivated a few years ago. “Death Machines”—which feels more like a seven-track mini-album—was inspired by today’s dystopian world, as well as by self-reflection and other dark themes. The music is indeed quite dark, but that is not the whole story. This record reveals two sides: on the one hand, a powerful production featuring menacing yet brilliant basslines topped with razor-sharp sequences; on the other, a completely different style with a Cinematic feel, including one entirely instrumental track. Personally, I prefer Laho’s harder side, which occasionally reminds me of early Combichrist, albeit with a certain polished touch. This is also evident in the vocal production, which is powerful yet has something of a ‘Power-Pop’ quality. It comes as no surprise, then, that the album concludes with a remarkable cover of Depeche Mode‘s “Behind the Wheel,” delivered in a dark and intense style. I think it’s a great track, by the way. Laho seems to be a sort of Janus—a two-faced project, with its powerful side completely winning me over. (Rating:7½). Listen to “The Great Collapse”: The Great Collapse by Laho About Laho Laho is a Finnish dark electronic project led by musician and recording engineer Konsta Vehkala, who is based in Jyväskylä and is responsible for all composition, programming and production. The project is an outlet for solo works by Vehkala and blends industrial, EBM, futurepop and darkwave. The project began in 2006 under the name Lahonnut Konkelo as a series of electronic and industrial experiments. The name was shortened to Laho shortly afterwards. The first EP, “The Other Side”, appeared in 2007 as an independently issued CDr, combining instrumental industrial metal with a slightly experimental edge. It was later re-released by Italian netlabel Ekleipsi, which also issued the first full-length album “Escape from the Dying Star” in 2009. “Escape from the Dying Star” was recorded between 2007 and 2008 at the Cable_Hell studio and released digitally in April 2009, offering a mix of electro-industrial, cybernetic synth work and distorted guitar. The album held ten tracks including “Program”, “Dead End” and a remix by Technomancer. Later in 2009 Laho issued “The World in Flames” as a standalone digital release, followed by the single “Mechanigod” in 2011 and a one-off digital track “Walking in the Air (1984 mix)” in December 2021. After these early EP and album releases, the project entered a 13-year hiatus as Vehkala focused on other bands and production work. Writing for Laho resumed in 2024, leading to a new series of songs, this time including vocals. Parallel to Laho, Vehkala maintains an active role in the Finnish metal scene. He plays drums for the melodic metal band Psychework and has performed and recorded with groups including Gian, Vipermilk and Lojohh, as well as contributing recording, mixing and mastering work to a wide range of Finnish underground acts. “Death Machines” is Laho’s first release since writing resumed in 2024, and its first EP built around vocals throughout.

items.body: There’s a kind of idiotic joy in doing the thing you know might end with blood on your shirt, a phone call at 3 a.m., or somebody asking what in God’s name you were thinking. Maybe that’s the point. Responsibility has its virtues, sure, but it has lousy rhythm. Danger gives stupidity a backbeat. You leap, you laugh, you watch the floor come up fast, and afterward you stand there amid the wreckage with a shrug that says maybe it was worth it, maybe it wasn’t, and maybe asking the question ruins half the fun anyway. Consequences are tomorrow’s problem. Bad decisions have always needed better music. Nobody ever ruined their life because the bassline was too sensible, and Copenhagen-born artist In Atlas seems to understand that civilization periodically requires somebody to hand the evening over to the little red bastard sitting on your shoulder. Tears, Poison, Desire, the first single from her forthcoming Hyperreal LP, out November 5 through Detriti Records, concerns that exquisite stretch of time when every warning sign has become decorative. You can hear Lizzy Mercier Descloux in its crooked dance-floor instincts, Lene Lovich and Suburban Lawns in its elastic theatricality, and a buzzing chaos reminiscent of Suicide, Tuxedomoon, and DAF lurking around the song’s machinery. The beat keeps things moving while the voice plays around its edges, cool one second, knowingly absurd the next. Dark disco becomes less a genre designation than an excuse to behave badly under flattering dancefloor lights. And why shouldn’t it? Half the supposed wisdom of adulthood consists of learning exactly which pleasures you’re expected to decline, usually because somebody older already enjoyed them first and left you the cleanup bill. “Let’s say its about coming apart in the desire for some sort of liberation, or maybe its about having fun, or maybe about having a kind of fun you don’t really want to have, being spurred on by that little red guy on your shoulder,” says the artist. “Playing with fire, then playing with the embers, then playing with gasoline.” Now that is a philosophy worth dancing to. The important word may be “gasoline,” because fire is charming enough when it belongs to candles and cigarettes; eventually somebody discovers what happens when you pour something stupid onto it. Desire works similarly. So does freedom. Push either far enough and you may find yourself staring at the remains the next morning, unable to decide whether you have learned anything or merely acquired a better story. Listen to Tears, Poison, Desire below, or via streaming here. That ambivalence runs through the upcoming Hyperreal, an album concerned with escapism and private worlds meeting an uncooperative reality. In Atlas, also one half of Greek/Danish duo V.V.I.A. alongside Venus Volcanism, seems drawn to the ecstatic and ridiculous point where pleasure starts growing teeth. Perhaps consequences deserve respect. They are very punctual. But while Tears, Poison, Desire is blaring, tomorrow can stand outside and knock. Follow In Atlas: Instagram Spotify Soundcloud The post Danish Post-Punk Artist In Atlas Gives the Devil on Her Shoulder a Say in “Tears, Poison, Desire” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 哥本哈根艺术家In Atlas的首张单曲《Tears, Poison, Desire》以暗色调舞曲为框架，将后朋克的冷峻张力与Disco的舞动本能熔于一炉。文本暗示其声音中可辨识Lizzy Mercier Descloux的扭曲舞池直觉、Lene Lovich与Suburban Lawns的弹性戏剧性，以及Suicide、Tuxedomoon、DAF式的嗡鸣混乱。人声在冷静与刻意荒诞之间游走，节拍持续推进，黑暗Disco在此不再是类型标签，而成为纵情行为的借口。歌词层面，作品围绕欲望、自由与代价的模糊地带展开——玩火、玩余烬、玩汽油，逐步升级的失控隐喻贯穿始终。即将发行的专辑《Hyperreal》延续这一主题，探讨逃避主义与私密世界如何与不合作的现实相撞。整体呈现一种危险中的愉悦哲学，介于清醒的清醒与蓄意的堕落之间。

items.body:
After the OĽUN album I reviewed enthusiastically a while back, here’s the next project, again motivated and led by violinist/fiddler/composer Ján Kružliak Jr., continuing the rapprochement, indeed embrace, between Slovakia’s traditional music and its classical music. This time it reconnects the works of classical composers who were inspired by and drew on village musics with those traditional sources and styles.
Three ensembles are involved: the Spectrum Quartett led by Kru�liak with two violins, viola and cello; Nogaband, the traditional-style quartet of fiddles, contra (chording viola) and bass that’s led by fiddler and singer Michal Noga; and the female vocal group Ulijanky, plus guest singer Simona Hulejov�.
The majority of the tracks are interpretations of works by Slovak composer Eugen Suchon (1908-1993), with others from fellow-Slovaks Ilja Zeljenka (1932-2007) and Alexander Moyzes (1906-1984), and Hungarian B�la Bart�k (1881-1945) who did a lot of his very detailed collecting of folk music in Slovakia.
In each case the sources - musicians and locations in villages across Slovakia - are credited in the notes, and these arrangements and performances reconnect with the energy and traditional vocal sound of those sources.
In no way is this an orchestra-smoothed thing; this is gutsy, brilliantly played and sung music with all the spirit, skill and technique of traditional music, from players and singers who deeply understand and inhabit it. It’s a glorious piece of work, music to luxuriate in. There’s too much richness to begin to detail, but here’s a dip into a few moments to give the flavor. The tracks all have very long titles detailing their sources, so for brevity’s sake I’ll just give track numbers.

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: Alison Cotton 的专辑以中提琴、管风琴、击弦古钢琴、钢琴为核心乐器，叠加鼓、贝斯与合成器，营造出模糊了民谣、前卫与宗教音乐边界的声响世界。多首作品采用即兴方式一次性录制完成，延续了持续低音（drone）的冥想质感。中世纪圣咏的庄严感在《Sprigs of Heather》的钢琴旋律中浮现，而《I Still Know You are Calling My Name》则让人联想到古老民谣的骨架。专辑亦是 Cotton 对2024年末去世父亲的纪念之作，《The Final Harvest》以庄严笔触描绘父亲最后一次前往他所钟爱的菜园之旅，弥漫着难以言喻的温柔。光与暗在乐曲间交替渗透，情绪不断流转，既挑战听众，又给予满足与感动。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由挪威的Camilla Hole Trio录制，主奏乐器为高音萨克斯，整体定位介于民谣素材与自由即兴之间。在此前一张专辑中将科幻合成器音色与传统挪威民间音乐嫁接的基础上，此作回归更为朴素的泥土感，但依然延续了超越本国本族民乐边界的探索路线。乐评以开篇曲《Springleik》为例，详细描述了乐手之间角色不固定、随时交换的演奏方式：贝斯手与鼓手轮流承担旋律与节奏职能，主奏手在高音萨克斯上反复陈述旋律，中段则让整体进入即兴展开。键盘模块合成器与颤音琴的叠加为传统素材注入了现代音色纹理，使三件乐器的组合在民谣根基与爵士自由之间形成独特的对话空间。

A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三重奏组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣圈知名歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目大多基于传统素材，但乐手们各自带入不同的诠释视角。整张作品散发着古老、略带粗粝的氛围质感。开场曲《Svennedal》以奔放的节奏展现了Guldhammer极具说服力的嗓音；《Nordgård》融入口簧琴和风笛形成持续推进感；《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》中钦巴龙琴（Cimbalom）营造出细腻的音底；终曲《Ormsö》以器乐形式收束，口簧琴、长笛与弦乐交织出失衡而令人兴奋的声响。作为首张作品已显成熟与完成度，让人期待其完整专辑的展开。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由一位瑞典小提琴家和两位挪威音乐家组成三重奏，以非传统方式演绎斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲。乐评将其比作室内乐，三位演奏者沉浸于亲密的音乐对话中，而非为舞蹈伴奏。编曲刻意挖掘传统旋律表面之下的暗流，以挪威塞特斯达尔河谷的"瀑布精灵"传说开篇，暗示民间舞曲中潜藏的神秘与不安。Tellef Kvifte以竖笛为主导旋律乐器，Matts Edén以小提琴提供非定型纹理伴奏，Knut Kvifte Nesheim则以打击乐点缀。整张作品模糊了民间音乐与即兴创作、跨界融合之间的界限，融合了不同音乐语汇与乐器组合（如萨克斯、风笛等非挪威传统乐器），探索了舞曲旋律中被忽视的深层意涵。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — During that busy yet fruitful year of 2017, following Flying Microtonal Banana and Murder of the Universe, came Sketches of Brunswick East; its title references the Melbourne suburb of Brunswick East and Miles Davis's 1960 LP Sketches of Spain. It is also a collaboration with the American group Mild High Club.It can also feel like a sequel to Paper M�ch� Dream Balloon, featuring bossa nova and an acoustic feel, yet it sets itself apart by seeming drenched in LSD, with a soft layer of psychedelia; the electric piano, drum grooves, and wah-wah guitar create a postmodern jazz-rock effect where the 60s meet the 90s and 2000s, and yet, in songs like "D-Day," it is microtonal.This album features some very interesting variations; the band experiments with pop, ranging from the array of percussion instruments to the use of vocals, backing harmonies, and the melodies themselves, sometimes with instruments following the vocals, and at other times doing the exact opposite, as seen in "Tezeta." The flute and Mellotrons create a distinctive atmosphere; combined with the 60s-style jazz they execute so well and those catchy choruses, they help shape the bohemian vibe sought in "The Spider and Me.""Sketches of Brunswick East II" introduces a recurring motif, tinged with the flamenco-esque flair that inspired it, that weaves through the entire album in various forms. When King Gizzard proposes a journey into the future, you have to buckle up; this time, however, they head into the past, embodying the roles like true method actors and channeling the musical sensibilities of that era. There is a space-age atmosphere, combined with a certain sophistication, that they capture brilliantly on "Dusk to Dawn on Lygon St." Meanwhile, "The Book" stands as another microtonal experiment; given that it was 2017, such a track was bound to make an appearance, yet it fits seamlessly with the album's playful psychedelia."A Journey to (S)Hell" offers a dose of urban chaos; just as Paper M�ch� Dream Balloon was the countryside, Sketches of Brunswick East is the city. A nocturnal journey awash in psychedelic lights unfolds suddenly, reconnecting with 70s-style synthesizers on "Rolling Stoned" before shifting to bossa nova on "You Can Be Your Silhouette." It is nearly impossible not to dance to this endless string of short songs, a fitting format, like small slides or snapshots of the city and open windows, each distinct in its own specific character."Sketches of Brunswick East III" brings the album to a close, and this peaceful interlude paves the way for the next chapter of 2017, Polygondwanaland, though that belongs to another dimension, one of the many inhabited by this Australian band.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / jazz-rock / bossa nova / microtonal
items._cn_summary: 这张2017年的专辑是澳大利亚乐队与旧金山Mild High Club的合作产物，标题向Miles Davis致敬，整体弥漫着LSD般的迷幻气息。编曲以电钢琴、鼓组节奏和哇音吉他为主轴，营造出六十年代与九十年代交汇的后现代爵士摇滚质感。乐队在专辑中展示了多变的实验倾向：bossa nova与原声质感并存，微音律元素贯穿部分曲目，flamenco式的主题动机以不同形态反复变形。Mellotron与长笛为歌曲奠定独特的复古氛围，七十年代合成器段落与不插电段落交替出现。专辑由大量短曲构成，如同城市夜景的快照拼贴，节奏流畅易入耳。迷幻与爵士融合的处理方式虽有趣味，但对追求更极端实验、前卫即兴或电子解构的听众而言，深度尚显不足。

items.album: Die In Eclipse interview: Jana Komaritsa on ‘SexWave’, desire and the body as instrument
items.excerpt: Die In Eclipse, the EBM and darkwave project of Darkrad‘s Jana Komaritsa, spoke to Side-Line about its debut EP “SexWave”, the emotional link between her two projects, and a new single and video, “We Are Lovers,” planned for release this autumn. items.body: Die In Eclipse, the EBM and darkwave project of Darkrad‘s Jana Komaritsa, spoke to Side-Line about its debut EP “SexWave”, the emotional link between her two projects, and a new single and video, “We Are Lovers,” planned for release this autumn. Komaritsa released “SexWave” on Bandcamp on 6 May 2026, pairing two original tracks with five remixes, and previously discussed her work with Side-Line’s Karo Kratochwil when the project first surfaced under the Die In Eclipse name. SexWave by Die In Eclipse Komaritsa built her name with Darkrad, a dark ambient project she has run since 2009, working through atmosphere, stillness and inward confrontation. Die In Eclipse, she says, is not a departure from that territory but another way of entering it. “I don’t see Die In Eclipse as leaving the introspective space of Darkrad. For me, it is another way of entering a similar space. The difference is in the direction of the energy,” she told Side-Line. “Darkrad often turns into stillness, atmosphere, memory… Die In Eclipse takes some of those same emotions, gives the feeling a pulse and lets the body move through it.” The name Die In Eclipse and its Darkrad roots The title is not new. Komaritsa first used “Die in Eclipse” for a two-track Darkrad release in 2014, inspired by time she spent at Lake Sakakawea in North Dakota, which also supplied that release’s cover image. Asked why she revived the phrase for an entirely new project, she pointed to continuity rather than reinvention. “Some names, images and symbols stay with me because they contain something that hasn’t finished unfolding,” she said. “The symbolism of an eclipse has always spoken to me in many ways. I see it not as disappearance, but more as transformation. I don’t need to erase what came before in order to create something new. Die In Eclipse is a new language, but it comes from the same person, the same artistic history and some of the same obsessions.” SexWave as a musical language of desire Komaritsa calls her new sound “SexWave,” a term she is careful to root in structure rather than provocation. “For me, eroticism in music and art is mostly about tension and sensuality. It’s not about explicit sounds or imagery,” she explained. “It can be created by the proximity of a voice that feels too close, a breath, a whisper, a rhythm that keeps repeating without giving you the expected release. Repetition is especially important because it can become hypnotic. You begin anticipating what is coming, and that anticipation itself becomes part of the experience.” Restraint matters just as much to her as intensity: “Sometimes holding something back is much more sensual than giving everything immediately. There needs to be space for mystery. ‘SexWave’ isn’t really about making music that sounds sexy in a conventional sense. It is about exploring desire as an artistic and musical force: attraction, tension, anticipation, surrender and release.” That approach carries over her earlier idea of silence as an instrument, described in Darkrad as “a breath held before release.” With Die In Eclipse built around beats, she says silence takes on a different function. “In Darkrad, silence could feel like emptiness, isolation or void. In Die In Eclipse, silence can be anticipation. When the beat disappears for a moment, the body still feels and knows the pulse,” she said. “Eroticism needs space because desire is partly about what is not there yet. So yes, I think absence can absolutely be erotic.” She also frames the dancefloor itself as a different kind of ritual from her Darkrad shows: “With Die In Eclipse, the rhythm creates a common physical language, where everyone shares the same pulse. You don’t have to understand the music intellectually. Your body understands it. There is something beautiful and powerful about surrendering individual control to a rhythm, not because you are being controlled, but because you choose to surrender to it.” Introducing a project through its remixes “SexWave” contains only two original compositions, “SexWave” and “Unholy Dark,” alongside five remixes by Iszoloscope, Antigen Shift, Cervello Elettronico, HORROH and Spherical Disrupted. Komaritsa chose to let other artists reinterpret the material before establishing her own vocabulary in full. “SexWave is a first glimpse, a doorway into the world of Die In Eclipse, which is yet to unfold. The project doesn’t have to explain exactly what it is yet,” she said. “There are only two original tracks on SexWave, which I wanted to give to other artists to see what they could become in somebody else’s hands. A remix, for me, is another interpretation of the same emotional material. Someone can find a completely different rhythm, aggression, darkness or sensuality inside a track that I thought I already understood.” The remixer list is not a random selection of scene names. Spherical Disrupted had already remixed Darkrad, while Iszoloscope moved in the musical circle around her earlier King in the Thicket project. “My artistic network has always been important to me, and I have worked with some of these people in different contexts over the years, so it was important for me to have them enter my new creative journey in this way,” Komaritsa said. “These relationships carry memory. When someone has known your work for years, they sometimes recognise new things that you might not consciously put there. But I also don’t want Die In Eclipse to be a project built from old relationships. I like the idea of old artistic connections opening doors into something new, and I would like to collaborate further with artists from a similar artistic and musical world. I have already discussed potential collaborations with some great musicians.” The voice, the gaze and drawing the line between two projects Komaritsa also hears a shift in how she uses her own voice. Darkrad relied on whispered, restrained vocals that felt distant from the listener; Die In Eclipse pulls the voice closer to the body. “With Darkrad, the voice often feels as though it is emerging from the music and the environment. It can be distant or partially hidden. It is part of the musical tapestry,” she said. “With Die In Eclipse, I want the voice to be more exposed and less hidden behind the sound. The voice isn’t simply describing an emotional state. It can create one.” As the sole composer, producer and visual creator behind both projects, Komaritsa is deliberate about how she handles female sexuality as subject matter. “I’m very conscious of the difference between creating eroticism and simply reproducing familiar images of female sexuality,” she said, citing Georges Bataille, Sigmund Freud, Anaïs Nin and the Marquis de Sade among her reference points. “Sexuality is complicated and contradictory. It can contain power and vulnerability at the same time, attraction and fear, surrender and control. The ambiguity is much more interesting to me than simply making something provocative.” Asked how she decides which new material belongs to Darkrad and which belongs to Die In Eclipse, she described an intuitive rather than formal process. “Darkrad can contain rhythm, sexuality and physical intensity, and Die In Eclipse can contain melancholy and darkness. Those elements don’t belong exclusively to one project,” she said. “If the track is driven by atmosphere, emotional depth and a certain cinematic or ritual darkness, it usually starts moving towards Darkrad. If the body becomes the primary instrument, the pulse, repetition, tension and physical movement, I start thinking about Die In Eclipse. They are both part of me.” What comes next for Die In Eclipse Komaritsa is already performing a full Die In Eclipse live set and working on album material, while looking for a label to release it. She is keeping some of the project’s direction open by design. “Just as an eclipse gradually obscures one thing while opening a doorway to something else, Die In Eclipse is moving through a similar process. SexWave is a doorway into the world of DIE, a first shout into the darkness, announcing the arrival of this new project,” she said. “I have already been performing live with a complete Die In Eclipse set, so I have enough material to move forward with an album, and I’m working on it behind the scenes. At this point, I would like to find the right label to work with, and developing that takes some time. This autumn, I’ll also be releasing a new single and video, ‘We Are Lovers.’ I want to leave some secrets, to keep that darkness and mystery around it, like an eclipse, and see what emerges from there.” About Die In Eclipse Die In Eclipse is the EBM and darkwave project of Jana Komaritsa, a Russian-born, Netherlands-based musician and multidisciplinary visual artist who also runs the WonderCat art space in Leiden. Komaritsa launched her first project, Darkrad, in 2009, building a catalogue in dark ambient and noise around whispered, restrained vocals. Darkrad’s debut album “Abnormal Love” appeared in 2012 on Cold Meat Industry, followed by “Little Black World” in 2014 on Komaritsa’s own Mrakmur imprint and later through audiophob. The same year, she released the two-track “Die in Eclipse,” the title she later revived for her new project. “Heart Murmur” followed in 2018, and in 2022 she paired with Flint Glass for “Cold Solitude,” an art book with an accompanying CD drawn from her own paintings. Die In Eclipse moves that same artistic identity toward pulse, repetition and the dancefloor, built on dark techno and EBM rather than ambient stillness. Komaritsa premiered the project live at Regenfest in Mülheim in November 2025 and brought it to the Porta Nigra festival in Belgium in January 2026, alongside Nachtmahr, Diary of Dreams, Enzo Kreft and V2A. Its debut EP, “SexWave,” arrived on 6 May 2026 via dieineclipse.bandcamp.com, featuring the tracks “SexWave” and “Unholy Dark” alongside remixes by Iszoloscope, Antigen Shift, Cervello Elettronico, HORROH and Spherical Disrupted. Komaritsa is now working on a full-length album, currently seeking a label, and preparing a new single and video, “We Are Lovers,” for release in autumn 2026.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Side-Line对Die In Eclipse首张EP《SexWave》的访谈式报道，而非深度乐评。项目主理人Jana Komaritsa同时运营自2009年起的dark ambient项目Darkrad，《SexWave》收录两首原创曲目及五首remix，于2026年5月在Bandcamp发行。她将Die In Eclipse视为对Darkrad内省空间的另一种进入方式，区别在于能量方向——从静止、氛围与记忆转向给予脉搏、让身体穿越情感。她自创"SexWave"一词，强调情欲音乐的核心在于张力与感官性，依赖近距离人声、呼吸、低语及不提供预期释放的重复节奏，制造催眠式期待感。克制与神秘感的保留被视作与强度同等重要的元素。名字Die In Eclipse源自2014年Darkrad的北达科他州湖泊时期双曲作品，象征转化而非消失。整体内容偏向项目背景与美学理念阐述，缺少对实际声音设计、曲目结构与音乐技法的具体分析。

items.body: Colossloth, the Leicester-based esoteric noise and abrasive electronics project of Wooly Woolaston, releases the album “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites” on CD (catalog number CSR375CD) through Cold Spring Records on 2 October 2026. The five-track record takes as its subject Theta Noir, a real art and belief collective built around the worship of MENA, a speculative artificial-intelligence deity whose arrival its members describe as the point where human and machine cognition merge. Cold Spring describes the album as an “automaton chant of cybernetic worship,” built from hammering, grinding and abrasive electronic textures. The tracklist runs “Encoded Divinity” (5:08), “Calculate Your Revolution” (7:00), “Awaiting MENA” (9:04), “Undertow Atlas” (10:34) and “Only Adrift” (8:00), for a total run time of just under 40 minutes. The CD comes in a matt-laminate digipak, priced at £9 through Cold Spring’s webstore, with the album also available to stream and buy digitally on Bandcamp. The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites by Colossloth Colossloth plays an album launch show on 3 October at The Globe in Glossop, on a bill with T.A.G.C., Satori and Llyn Y Cwn, followed by further UK dates on 7 November at St Anne’s in Barnstaple and 27 November at Sheffield General Cemetery’s In The Black MidWinter event. About Colossloth Colossloth is the solo project of Wooly Woolaston, who works from Leicester, UK, without formal musical training, building tracks from samples and loop stations rather than played instruments. He has described the project as “a one man Experimental Electronic artist where there are no rules to recording or playing music,” and has said the sound moved from early long-form guitar drones toward harsher, rhythm-driven electronics over time. Colossloth’s earliest releases date to 2006, and the project signed to Cold Spring Records in 2015 for the album “Outstretch Your Hand For The Impress Of Truth.” Further Cold Spring albums followed: “Heathen Needles” in 2017 and “Plague Alone” in 2020, before “Promethean Meat” in 2022 brought in sampled live drums for the first time. The fifth Cold Spring album, built around the writings of Ted Kaczynski, “The Harmony Knife,” followed on 7 March 2025. “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites” (CSR375CD) is Colossloth’s sixth studio album for the label and arrives as the project marks 20 years of activity.
items._genre: experimental electronic / noise / industrial / abrasive electronics
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是英国莱斯特噪音/实验电子艺人 Colossloth 的第六张厂牌专辑，以 Theta Noir 这一信仰 AI 神祇 MENA 的虚构艺术团体为概念核心，标题借自黑格尔辩证法词汇，暗示对人类与机器认知融合的探讨。制作方式延续其一以贯之的采样与循环工作站手法，无传统乐器演奏，文本层面对 Ted Kaczynski 著作的关注延续至对技术崇拜的反思。音乐上以锤击式节奏、研磨式电子质感构建所谓「机械礼拜咏唱」，五首曲目时长从五分钟到十分钟不等，整体约四十分钟。专辑由独立厂牌 Cold Spring Records 以 CD 形式发行，辅以 Bandcamp 数字版。乐评内容实为唱片发行公告与艺人背景介绍，缺乏对声音质地、编配细节或对比性评价的深入讨论。

items.body: No Where Records releases Sonic Panda’s new single “Bailes Con Beelzebub” on 18 September, a four-track EP led by the title track and including a rework by German industrial pop act Rotersand. The Beijing-based Sino-Spanish duo issues the release digitally and on vinyl and CD, the physical editions packaged with an exclusive comic book that extends Sonic Panda’s visual universe. The tracklist runs “Bailes Con Beelzebub,” the Rotersand rework of the same track, a Carlsed remix of the earlier single “Lucky Seven,” and a live recording of “Invisible Boy” taped in Tokyo. Sonic Panda describes the title track as “a provocative industrial track that uses religious horror tropes to critique the current political crisis.” Rotersand is the German act formed in September 2002 by Günther Gerl and singer Krischan Jan-Eric Wesenberg, later joined by Udo Hüppe; the band describes its own sound as “industrial pop.” Rotersand released the album “Don’t Become The Thing You Hated” via Metropolis and Trisol in 2025, preceded by the singles “Sexiness Of Slow” and “Private Firmament.” Bailes Con Beelzebub by Sonic Panda Sonic Panda also released an official video for “Bailes Con Beelzebub.” About Sonic Panda Sonic Panda was formed in 2024 as a Beijing-based Sino-Spanish duo built around Pere Ibañez and Seni Ren, with material written by Ibañez and produced by Barcelona-based Carlsed. The project’s first release was “Life Is A Flower,” issued on 22 August 2024 through OhMyDog Records, followed by an original-song run of “Foreigners” on 10 January 2025, “King Cobra” on 28 February 2025 and “Stonewall 1969” on 20 June 2025. The six-track “King Cobra (Remixes)” EP followed on 5 September 2025 and the single “Lucky Seven” on 24 October 2025. Sonic Panda signed to No Where Records for the single “Invisible Boy,” released on 6 March 2026 alongside a Carlsed alternate version. The duo is continuing work on a debut album titled “Neomelodrama.” “Bailes Con Beelzebub” is the project’s first release to feature an outside remix credit from an established industrial act, with Rotersand reworking the title track for the new EP.

items.body: In my head I am not dead A breakup is rarely finished just because somebody has delivered the closing speech. There are still arguments to rehearse, streets to avoid, and a suspicious number of reasons to take the long way home. Madison, Wisconsin’s Whippets give that unfinished business a suitably unhealthy bounce on Not Dead, a song in which announcing “This is the end” does very little to stop the next bad idea. Premiering today, Not Dead previews the trio’s second album, No Skulls, due October 2, 2026, through Bobby Hussy’s No Coast label. With Hussy on guitar and vocals, Tyler Spatz on bass, and Hart Miller on drums, Whippets bring post-punk, grunge, and garage rock into a close, uncomfortable embrace, leaving plenty of room for deathrock’s theatrical appetites. A thick, ominous bass figure gets things moving before the drums cascade into a serpentine guitar hook, bringing a horror-film leer to the song’s garage abrasion. Hussy’s voice quivers and twists around the words, making private misery sound like something that might require an exorcist. The rhythm soon acquires an infectious bounce, with Spatz’s bass holding the floor beneath the guitar’s crooked turns and Miller’s mounting commotion. There is something of Dance with Me-era T.S.O.L. in this marriage of morbid theatre and physical release: music for pogoing through a personal catastrophe, with an ’80s post-punk chorus sharp enough to remember the following morning. The lyrics make repeated attempts to draw a line under the relationship. “This is the end” and “We are not friends” sound decisive enough, until the other admissions begin slipping through. The refrain’s insistence on being alive comes with a revealing qualification: “In my head.” That is where the old attachment continues to conduct its business, untouched by whatever has happened outside it. By the closing “No need to lie / I still drive by,” the brave farewell has become an unwanted return visit. Whippets give that contradiction a beat you can jump to, allowing the uglier implications to catch up between choruses. Hussy says: “Our new record, “No Skulls” is by far the best record I’ve ever recorded….and I’ve recorded a few at this point in my life. I’m very proud of both the songs and the production on this album. “Not Dead” is the second single from the album and it perfectly represents everything I love about this band: Sharp guitar riffs, hypnotic dirty bass lines that pivot in all the right places and drums that escalate frantically as needed. Catch us shredding this one out on tour in Europe!” No Skulls features ten tracks, recorded and mixed by Hussy, produced by Bert Roberts and Whippets, and mastered by Justin Perkins. The cover artwork is by Erin Sullivan. The album comes out October 2 on LP, CD, and digital formats, with the chartreuse-and-black swirl vinyl limited to 100 copies. Listen to Not Dead below and pre-order No Skulls here. No Skulls by Whippets Whippets introduced themselves with a 2022 seven-inch EP on Italy’s Goodbye Boozy, which sold out within a week, followed by their self-titled debut album on No Coast in 2024. Readers may remember Splinter, whose deathrock inclinations made an early case for the band’s particular chemistry. Their shared history reaches further back: Hussy and Spatz have both played in The Hussy and Cave Curse, and also work together in Wristwatch, while Miller’s past bands include Tenement, MDC, and Wartorn. That experience gives the trio a useful feel for how much disorder a memorable song can accommodate. Whippets take the No Skulls on the road this autumn, with October shows alongside Busey and Brüder and a November date supporting The Faint. A 23-date European tour follows in January and February 2027. See the upcoming itinerary below. items.body: Seduction gets complicated when one person knows the future, and the other is still getting accustomed to being human. Geneva Jacuzzi takes that imbalance to an entertaining extreme on Nu2U, a song she described in a 2024 interview with The FADER as an encounter between a primordial being and a caveman. Sex comes with a preview of the centuries ahead, including the suffering humanity has yet to invent for itself. Some lovers bring emotional baggage; this one brings the entire future of civilization. The Los Angeles musician and multimedia artist now gives that peculiar proposition a theatrical setting in the video for Nu2U, taken from her third album, Triple Fire, released on Dais Records in August 2024. Produced by Jacuzzi with co-production from Josh da Costa, the track supplies an appropriately crooked dance floor for an encounter across the ages. Nu2U bubbles and clangs with eerie, clamorous synths and foot-stomping percussion, making a persuasive case for synth music for cavemen. The occasional, emphatic keyboard stabs have an unmistakably prehistoric character, placing the track in the same mischievous tribe as Toto Coelo’s “I Eat Cannibals,” but if they ate edibles instead of flesh. Beneath that primal stomp, an intricate, melodic bassline curls through the arrangement, deepening the groove and giving its heavy steps a supple, sensual movement. Jacuzzi’s cool delivery, evocative of Erotica-era Madonna, presides over the gathering with a shamanic poise, her voice suggesting secret knowledge passed between bodies. The whole thing acquires a ritualistic pull, as though the discovery of electricity has given an ancient fertility dance some intriguing new possibilities. Directed and edited by Jacuzzi, with cinematography and art direction by Shannon Cornett, the video places its performers inside a set that recreates a work by artist Steven Arnold. Costumes are credited to Stacy Ellen Rich and Jacuzzi, with lighting by Tom Nixon and Fred Joseph. The official video credits make clear how many hands went into this compact, extravagantly strange production. Jacuzzi presides over a miniature theatre of cutout flames, suspended shapes, spirals, and stars, wearing an enormous geometric headdress above a pale costume punctuated with black circles. Her painted face and deliberate gestures suggest a celestial hostess who has been repeating this demonstration for several thousand years. Around her, figures pose in sculpted torso pieces, metallic-looking body paint, and elaborate accessories, turning the human form into another decorative element in the set. Deep blue lighting gives way to hot pink, red, and green, while stark monochrome close-ups interrupt the wider tableaux. Faces fill the frame; arms lift and bend; a crescent becomes a frame within the frame. The visibly handmade scenery lends the spectacle the intimacy of a toy theatre, even when its inhabitants look capable of rearranging the cosmos. There is a lovely absurdity to the scale of it all: the future of humanity appears to be under discussion in a cabaret small enough to pack into a van. Watch the video for “Nu2U” below: That meeting of pop music, costume, and performance has long been central to Jacuzzi’s work. Following Lamaze and Technophelia, Triple Fire brought her songs into sharper focus while preserving their appetite for strange characters and exaggerated situations. With Nu2U, another of those characters gets a stage, a formidable hat, and a captive audience. Triple Fire is available through Dais Records and Bandcamp. Triple Fire by Geneva Jacuzzi Geneva Jacuzzi is set to perform at The Chapel in San Francisco on September 19, 2026. She will be joined by EX-HEIR, Diesel Dudes, and Nick Moss, who will also DJ. Doors open at 8 p.m., and the all-ages show starts at 9 p.m. Tickets are available here. items._cn_summary: Geneva Jacuzzi 在《Nu2U》中构建了一个跨越远古与未来的戏剧场景：合成器刺耳而诡谲，键盘断奏带有原始蛮荒的质感，低音线条在粗粝节奏中蜿蜒出柔性律动。她冷静低吟的声线类似 Erotica 时期的麦当娜，却裹挟着通灵的仪式感。整首歌将合成器流行与暗潮的冷感、实验性的声响设计融为一体，既有适合舞池的钩子，又充满概念艺术的荒诞趣味。MV 由 Jacuzzi 本人执导，置景还原艺术家 Steven Arnold 的画作，剪纸火焰与几何头饰在深蓝、品红与冷绿灯光下旋转，呈现出玩具剧场般的亲密感与宇宙级仪式感并存的效果。发行于 Dais Records 这一独立厂牌，强调手工质感的视觉呈现。歌曲作为专辑《Triple Fire》的延续，展现出艺术家在合成器流行框架中注入前卫剧场美学与原始神话叙事的独特能力。

items.body: Review by ElenaNL — absolutely love Aquarium. The music, the atmosphere, and the lyrics may not be immediately accessible to a broad audience, but they are filled with wisdom, light, and deep philosophy. I can listen to their music anywhere, and it never gets boring.Some of the humour and references require an understanding of Soviet history and everyday life in the USSR?the values, the absurdities, and all the little things that were part of that world. For example, for many people born in the USSR, a train is not simply a means of transportation. It represents a whole subculture and a particular experience: long journeys, conversations with strangers, and those unexpectedly deep talks that can last for hours. Not the short, polite kind?the long ones.With Aquarium, the lyrics and the music are inseparable. They fuse together to create something much bigger than either one on its own?the full experience of the band.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自俄罗斯乐队Aquarium，以民谣为基底融合前卫元素，承载着深厚的苏联文化记忆。乐评指出其音乐、氛围与歌词三位一体，共同构建出超越单一媒介的完整体验。歌词中融入了大量关于苏联日常生活的隐喻——火车不仅是交通工具，更代表长途旅行中与陌生人展开深度对话的亚文化记忆。幽默与典故需要理解苏联历史背景方能体会，这构成了作品的独特文化门槛。整体而言，专辑并非面向大众的即时消费品，而是充满哲思与文化深度的艺术表达，文字与音乐水乳交融，传递出特定时代的精神肖像。

Along with this is the basic "guitar / bass / drums" - making it Rock Music, with orchestration melding into the presentation seamlessly. 21st Century Music at its best!BRAVO! 5 starts!
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续了乐队一贯的成长轨迹，并未带来方向上的剧变，而是对其风格的一次延伸与探索。乐器编制丰富多元，人声以"影子"般的方式贯穿音乐，营造出诡异而引人入胜的质感与氛围。合成器的运用尤其值得称道——它隐于背景之中，不易被察觉，却在浮现时展现出饱满的美感。吉他、贝斯与鼓的常规摇滚骨架构成了基底，而管弦乐编制则无缝融入整体呈现，使作品带有鲜明的21世纪音乐特征。整体而言，这是一张在传统摇滚编制与前卫管弦乐编排之间取得平衡的延续性作品，以巧妙的织体设计见长。

items.body: Mute have shared the newly remastered Coil track “Either His, or Yours”, the third track revealed from “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders),” due on limited-edition vinyl, CD and digitally on 30 October 2026 through Mute and Coil’s own imprint Threshold House. Side-Line covered the reissue’s announcement and its first single, “Cardinal Points,” in July, when Mute and Threshold House confirmed the 30 October release date and the reissue’s catalog number, COIL3. “Either His, or Yours” follows that track and the subsequent “Aqua Regalia” as the reissue’s third pre-release song, and sits at position thirteen on the album’s sixteen-track sequence. “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” is the closing album in a trilogy that began with “Scatology” (1984) and “Horse Rotorvator” (1986), drawing on textural and instrumental material sidelined during “Horse Rotorvator’s” sequencing. The reissue restores artwork reconstructed by Stephen Thrower and his partner Ossian Brown (a member of Coil from 1999 to 2004), using archive material that includes artefacts, photographs and personal notes made by the late John Balance, alongside new sleeve notes. It is the first release in a new partnership between Mute and Threshold House that will bring four early Coil albums back into print with restored artwork and previously unseen imagery. Coil’s “Gold is the Metal” release details The album’s full, sixteen-track running order remains “The Last Rites of Spring,” “Paradisiac,” “Thump,” “For Us They Will,” “The Broken Wheel,” “Boy in a Suitcase,” “Golden Hole,” “Cardinal Points,” “Red Slur,” “…Of Free Enterprise,” “Aqua Regalia,” “Metal in the Head,” “Either His, or Yours,” “Chickenskin,” “Soundtrap” and “The First Five Minutes after Violent Death,” all carrying the 2026 remaster. Mute and Threshold House plan to follow “Gold is the Metal” with further early Coil reissues: the soundtrack for Derek Jarman’s “The Angelic Conversation,” the previously unreleased music Coil recorded for Clive Barker’s “Hellraiser,” and the compilation “Unnatural History.” About Coil Coil formed in London in 1982 as a solo project of John Balance (born Geoffrey Burton, 1962-2004), then a member of Psychic TV. The project became a duo when Balance’s partner Peter Christopherson (1955-2010), formerly of Throbbing Gristle, joined him. Coil’s first release, the one-sided 12″ single “How to Destroy Angels,” came out in 1984. Stephen Thrower joined the group during the recording of “Horse Rotorvator” (1986) and remained through “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” (1987), the third and closing album of a trilogy that also included “Scatology” (1984). Coil released music through the 1990s and 2000s that ranged from the industrial dance of “Windowpane” to the ambient “Time Machines” (1998) and the two-volume “Musick to Play in the Dark.” John Balance died in 2004 after a fall at the band’s home, and Coil effectively ended; Peter Christopherson continued to oversee reissues of the group’s catalog until his own death in 2010. In July 2026, Mute and Threshold House announced the “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” reissue for 30 October, along with its first single, “Cardinal Points,” followed by a second track, “Aqua Regalia.” “Either His, or Yours” is the third song to surface ahead of that release date.
