items.body: I’ll admit, the announcement of a new Uncle Acid and the deadbeats album hardly registered with me. It’s been a damn long while since I’ve had them in regular rotation, as I sorta fell off after 2015’s The Night Creeper. Not that that record really spoiled anything for me—it just didn’t seem to do anything that my favorites, Blood Lust and Mind Control, hadn’t already handled better. That said, it took almost a decade for them to catch my ear again, this time with the (respectfully) weird and adventurous detour of 2024’s mostly instrumental Nell’ Ora Blu. Its soundtrack-y, synth-forward nature showcased the group as genuinely astute mood-setters, even if it ultimately felt more suited to passive listening than the kind of record I’d actively return to. Still, it was enough to remind me that there’s something uniquely compelling about the way Uncle Acid and the deadbeats can set a tone—and maybe that I’d been a little too quick to give up on them.While their occult proto-metal contemporaries Ghost shapeshifted from similar stripped-down beginnings to achieve varying degrees of critical success and significant popularity, I’ve always felt that UA’s comparatively reserved, less immediately theatrical approach offered more potential. Where Ghost have increasingly embraced the spectacle and lore, UA hit me as less clownish and gimmicky, finding ways to be genuinely unsettling and music-focused without resorting to this razor-blade-in-my-Halloween-candy sort of Trojan-horsing Satan into pop music that everyone seems to find so clever. So I admit, I have a little rooting interest and bias here. Not that this guided my listening so much as brought to light an interesting contrast in how things just happen to shake out sometimes. I’m not passing judgment on either approach or trying to yuck anyone’s yums, I just find it curious how what seemed to be similar bands a decade-and-a-half ago have taken such different paths. Shapes Of Midnight by Uncle Acid and the deadbeats So, that leaves us with actually getting into Shapes Of Midnight and where UA find themselves in 2026. While some bands trickle in new flavors over time, their hard pivot on Nell’ Ora Blu, though head-scratching at the time, nicely paves the way for Shapes Of Midnight. Here, the analog synths and horns are again essential, coloring a more metal-forward (oh, we’re beyond proto-metal now, babes) sound while also establishing these textures as something utterly integral to the UA sound, making them sound fuller and more complete and compelling than ever.The title track is a prime example, delivering that signature UA haunted bounce, recalling one of my all-time faves from Mind Control, “Poison Apple,” here with synths lending a cosmic warmth akin to Zombi that significantly ups the ante on the spooky factor. This fuller, more robust sound enhances their more metallic edge on this go, even with some Thin Lizzy-esque harmonies and more nuanced, detailed songwriting. Still catchy as all get-out, thankfully, but structurally, Shapes Of Midnight has way more meat on its bones, earning every second on the record’s longer compositions. The melodies, while a strong point on previous records, are at full-tilt here in many forms. B-side opener “Psycho on the Loose” delivers a well-timed 80s metal gut- punch in the vein of Judas Priest with one of the best hooks of their entire discography. Similarly, “Don’t Let It Control You” finds a surfy, classic rock ‘n’ roll backbone where keys bang away, and yet again, the way things come together feels so right, not homage-y, schtick-y, or experimental, but rather that UA is just dripping in such rich horror and throwback atmosphere that the juxtaposition of these tracks doesn’t even make me flinch.The pieces they've put into motion and the world they’ve built over the last couple records feels like it’s fully realized here. “When Evil Wakes” gives the synths and horns even more room to shine, hitting this sort of Doors-y stride, even dipping toes in a pitch-black boogie before gathering steam and building to a Sabotage-era Black Sabbath peak where leads flirt and dance around one another, richly layered vocals froth up a hypnotic haze, acoustic guitars lend a metallic ring, and the bass and drums lock into a groove both nimble and rock solid. It’s an early highlight representative of their comfort, confidence, and vision. “The Other Side of the Sky” connects with another stellar metal hook, matching this buzzy, near-sci-fi synth with a cowbell-laden stomp that will satisfy Mountain fans. Bigger yet is “I Won’t Sleep (‘til You’re Gone)” which captures glam and psychedelia through a veil of sepia-tinged goth rock, boasting bombasts of horns that are as infectious as they are curious—it’s almost surprising there’s not an Iggy Pop guest spot on this track. It’s sassy, sultry, and downright chilling. (“We’ll be turning the soil while your bones start to boil on the stove”? Oof!) Again, the production is phenomenal, every element hits with clarity, power, and purpose. Truly and expertly orchestrated.Ultimately, Shapes Of Midnight offers a complete, well-rounded, and fully actualized version of the Uncle Acid we’ve all …kind of… heard before. The retro flavors are absolutely on point with the additional instrumentation, the songwriting is as sharp as ever, and the horror storytelling inspired by Poe’s The Masque of the Red Death offers depth and intrigue. It’s exactly what I didn’t know I had been waiting for, and by the time the oddly bluesy, almost Danzig-esque closer “Sleep No More” drives its artful and unnerving final nail in the coffin, Shapes Of Midnight has revealed itself as not just a fantastic record in its own right, but also as the culmination of years of harrowing work. (Un)Safe to say, the time to reconnect with your old Uncle Acid has never been better.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑标题本身即为一场文字游戏：T.I.M.既可解读为Tall, Infinite, Microscopic，也可延伸为Till Immediate Meditation或Tomorrow is Minimalist，模糊性本身就是对乐队创作理念的暗示。他们将极为广泛的素材与影响并置融合，让每一种来源都保留其原始特征，在共存中形成张力。然而原文仅为简短摘录，实际的音乐手法、编配细节、演奏者构成等信息均未展开，仅凭标题与简介难以判断其声学落点究竟落在实验即兴、电子氛围、还是简约主义一端。小众厂牌BMC Records的出身暗示其面向先锋听众，但本文作为乐评的有效内容过于稀薄，无法构成有意义的审美判断。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — The first BS &T album I bought. I found it greatly disappointing but it served my musical education process by helping me to define the kind of musics I did not like. 1. "Hi De Ho" (4:25) never a favorite of mine though I recognize the talent, skill, and hard work that went into pulling this one off. (8.75/10)2. "The Battle" (2:43) the harpsichord opening and recorder joining in as Steve Katz provides the serious vocals of this anachronistic tune. Inspired by THE ASSOCIATION's "Requiem for the Masses"? I've always liked the Baroque Revival trend of the 1960s. (9.125/10) 3. "Lucretia MacEvil" (3:03) trying to make more out of the success of "Spinning Wheel." Great performances but, come on, Guys! Once is enough! (8.875/10)4. "Lucretia's Reprise" (2:35) now, isn't this a little embarrassing and tacky?! Two times through the same song (though this one is less "Spinning Wheel" and more Brass-Rock expos�. And, yes, David really does let his full TOM JONES come shining through. (9/10)5. "Fire and Rain" (4:02) trying to make James Taylor's masterful and iconic tune more serious, more poignant. I can understand but this is the kind of stuff that should be saved for live concert encores. I'm not really a fan of the brassification of the tune, either. (8.875/10)6. "Lonsome Suzie" (4:35) piano jazz-blues over which David shows off his softer, subtler LOU RAWLS side. The soft, subtle horn arrangements are quite a sublime touch but the rest is kind of . . . unnecessary. (8.75/10)7. "Symphony for the Devil/Sympathy for the Devil" (7:49) now this is an interesting version/take on an all-time rock classic. It feels quite a bit like Andrew Lloyd Weber's material for Jesus Christ Superstar, which was written and partly recorded and being rehearsed when BS&T were recording the songs for this album. In fact, many of the themes and palettes seem to mirror the JCS album quite directly--despite the fact that JCS didn't get released until October of 1970. (BS&T 3 was released by Columbia Records in June of 1970.) So, which came first? Were BS&T playing this in their controversial European tour during the fall and winter of 1969 and 1970? I do, in fact, really like this rendering of of the Stones iconic song--maybe even better than the original (especially the "Sympathy for the Devil" half). (13.5/15)8. "He's A Runner" (4:15) my favorite song on the album, it's a cover of a Laura Nyro composition, there's just such a cool lounge vocal jazz vibe to this music and these performances, start to finish--like real professionals of the club scene, American and European. (9.5/10)9. "Somethin' Comin' On" (4:33) my second favorite song on the album. It's a cover of a Joe Cocker tune. Too bad when I was young I never gave this album's Side Two much attention cuz as I hear it now I hear/feel the best of this band as well as the best of the Brass Rock phenomenon. It's as if they've snuck Terry Kath to sing over the BS&T band's music while using both Chicago and BS&T's horn players. I love Halligan's organ play. (9.25/10)10. "40,000 Headmen" (4:40) a really interesting multi-part song attributed to the unknown Fred Lewis, it's got slow sections, child lullaby sections, brass rock passages, and lively uptempo jazz-rock parts. Great song! All hail Side Two! (9.125/10)Total time: 42:20A-/4.5 stars; despite the mostly flat renderings of the (to me) questionable song choices and Side One, the album only gets stronger as it leaves its "Spinning Wheel" past behind and chooses to explore its own preferred styles (on Side Two). For such a talented band I wish they could/would consider writing and exposing their own writing material and not just rely on covers. I find myself reluctant to include this album in the context of a pop or prog or even Jazz-Rock Fusion domain but it does contain some really finely crafted songs.
items._cn_summary: 这是Blood, Sweat & Tears第三张专辑的乐评，作者逐曲分析了专辑的编曲与人声表现。专辑以铜管摇滚为核心框架，融合爵士、蓝调、巴洛克复辟元素和大乐队编制。David Clayton-Thomas的演唱风格在Tom Jones式的爆发力与Lou Rawls式的柔和之间切换，部分曲目试图将流行摇滚经典（James Taylor的Fire and Rain）重新演绎为更严肃的版本。作者对专辑整体评价偏低，认为虽有技艺但缺乏个人特色，更像是商业铜管摇滚的典型产物。其中对滚石名曲Sympathy for the Devil的改编是亮点，呈现出与Jesus Christ Superstar相似的音乐语言。该专辑属于1970年代美国主流厂牌发行的商业融合爵士摇滚作品，与实验前卫、学术爵士、电子等方向相距较远。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — When your album is from 1970 and you manage to sound more stoned than your contemporaries, you're ahead in at least one area. This debut from DANDO SHAFT, while not actually a concert album in spite of the implications of its title, possesses a live feel that vacillates both shakily and tightly in at the intersection of JETHRO TULL, MOODY BLUES, JAN DUKES DE GREY, MUSHROOM, with a wink or two to FUCHSIA (which they do nonetheless predate) and LINDISFARNE. In all, this is, while not quite a missing link, a varied and more than competent collection with a few surprises to maintain freshness after so many decades, achieved through the harmony vocals, Celtic flourishes and just enough psych to keep the folk-weary from unhinging a jaw. To get a flavor for the best on offer here from the integrated styles, go for the EMTIDI-like "September Wine", the reflective ballad "In the Country", and the twangy and uplifting "End of the Game". Don't dismiss the later bonus tracks either if you can connect with then, but most of all, give this one a p.m with whatever comfort consumable you've been saving.
items._genre: prog folk / psychedelic folk / celtic folk
items._cn_summary: 这张1970年的前卫民谣专辑展现了英式民谣摇滚的典型面貌，融合了Jethro Tull式的器乐编排与Moody Blues的和声传统。凯尔特民谣元素以点缀形式出现，配合适度的迷幻色彩，整体呈现出松弛而略带迷醉的现场感。和声演唱是专辑的核心特色，几首推荐曲目如'September Wine'带有德式民谣的简约气质，'In the Country'是内省的抒情曲，'End of the Game'则偏向明亮跳跃。整体而言，这是一张技艺扎实但风格相对传统的民谣专辑，未触及实验音乐、爵士即兴或电子声响的边界，与当代前卫、实验或世界音乐融合路线的交集有限。

items.body: Review by Radisa50 — LP "Time" is the first album of the Zagreb rock group Time, recorded in the Jadran film studio in Dubrava, Zagreb, in April 1972, published by Jugoton in August 1972 (runout 160772), in many respects it is a copy and plagiarism of the music of the English progressive jazz-rock group Colosseum, and mostly the composition from their 2LP "Colosseum Live" from 1971.For the musical introduction of the song "For the life I was born into/Za koji ?ivot treba da se rodim"", the introduction of the composition "Walking In The Park" was taken literally, and in its sequel, such phrases from "Skelington" were plagiarized for the riffs!Also, "Hegedupa Upa" is nothing but a filler, an addition to the album, based on the playing of themes from "Colosseum Live", after all, like all Time album arrangements from that Colosseum live album.In a statement for Svet 1995, Dado Topić indirectly confirmed the copying of Colosseum when he said: "But the key moment was when we played in Zagreb's Dom of Sports as an opening act for the famous band 'Koloseum'." They sounded exactly the way I wanted 'Time' to sound."Also Time would not only not have been called that, but also would not have had Colosseum as a musical matrix if it had not been suggested by their future producer Vladimir Mihaljek Miha.He helped Dad Topić to create a new group after leaving the first Yugoslav progressive rock group Korni grupa in Belgrade.Namely, Miha appeared at a moment when Dado was helpless because the realization of the idea to reactivate Osijek's Dynamites was not possible.And not just gathering, creating a group, but also what and how to play, whose matrix to use.This conclusion was confirmed by Zlatko Gal in the accompanying text for the reissue of the album Time 2019 when he wrote: "Listening to what is happening on the global scene, which has been networked by prog-rock supergroups, but also the situation on the home ground, Mihaljek correctly concluded that the moment is right for a domestic response as well. And guessed!" Yes, he guessed by giving them the musical matrix of the then dominant English progressive rock group Collosseum!And not only did they plagiarize, they called themselves Time based on the name of Colosseum's third studio album "Daugher Of Time" from the summer of 1970, as well as the composition from that record "Time Machine" and the opening song of the first Time album "Istina ma?ina" is a consequence of that inspiration.By the way, Dado Topić was not telling the truth when he said that Time was the opening act for the Colosseum concert in the Zagreb Sports Hall.That English jazz-rock group was indeed a guest in Zagreb, but as Colosseum II with a concert in the Dom sportova on Sunday, September 26, 1976. as part of a three-day YU tour. Journalist Ante Batinović in a detailed review of that concert held in Studio be. 651 of 25. IX 1976 nowhere mentions any pre-group, and therefore neither Time as Dado asserted, of course wrongly, not to say falsely. Evaluate album?The studio performance of the Time album is impeccable, and if it weren't for the aggravating circumstances of the composition, i.e. the plagiarism of Colosseum, that album would deserve the highest rating.Their poor live performance of "Za koji ?ivot..." at the Pop Festival Ljubljana 72-BOOM, held on April 20 and 21, 1972, is also aggravating. This cannot serve to honor the great musicians of the Time group.
items._cn_summary: 这张1972年发行的专辑来自克罗地亚萨格勒布的Time乐队，是南斯拉夫早期前卫摇滚的重要文献。然而乐评的核心论点并非艺术分析，而是指控该作品系统性地抄袭英国爵士摇滚乐队Colosseum的作品，包括《Colosseum Live》中的段落、riff甚至连乐队名称都源自Colosseum的专辑《Daughter of Time》。文中引用了制作人Mihaljek和成员Dado Topić的访谈，以及2019年再版的附文，说明乐队在音乐方向和命名上均受Colosseum影响。文末还纠正了Dado关于乐队曾为Colosseum暖场的说法，指出该次演出实际是Colosseum II在1976年的巡演。整个评论聚焦于抄袭争议与历史考据，而非音乐本身的艺术价值或创新性。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — An American band that has both an unusual back story as well as quite the unusual motivation. Veterans who are somehow collectively inspired to represent and express a blend of Spanish colonizer and Native American tradition, mythos, and spirit.1. "(Intro) The Coming Of The Spaniards" (3:54) Alan Parsons Project-like Western choir mixed into a musical pastiche that sounds like something from a Spanish "spaghetti western" like soundtrack. It's like throwing APP together with Novella-era RENAISSANCE. Powerful and most excellent! (9.667/10)2. "The Benefits Of Breathing Quietly" (5:56) excellent piano-based APP prog over which singers John Baker and Jake Livgren provide some excellent, appropriately bombastic vocals--entwined and mutually supportive. The music is excellent, the story in the lyrics powerful, the overall effect quite emotional. This is the kind of music and song that reaffirms the reason prog exists! And this Lisa LaRue: She is a FORCE! (9.333/10)3. "The Plains? Truth" (6:49) an instrumental symphonic rock soundscape that reminds me of the best of bands like Kansas, The Dregs, and modern day Prog Folk band SOLSTICE. Excellent programming and computer-generated violin--and sound engineering! Lisa: Maestra: you are nothing short of a genius! This is great prog! (14/15)4. "Quivira Bound" (5:33) this one feels more like old prog, old classic rock. Bombastic opening with piano-based lull for John and Jake's vocal presentation to begin in, we quickly find ourselves back in classic STYX/SOLSTICE/IONA/DAVE BAINBRIDGE/ALAN PARSONS PROJECT territory though, of course, you have to substitute male vocal tracks for most of the female ones--and EXCELLENT are the performances of both John and Jake. Though John Baker's choice of electric guitar tone is a little odd, it works well enough to take nothing away from Lisa's excellent music. (9/10)5. "Moving Forward" (6:51) an instrumental of exemplar weave of prog solos, violin, real and otherwise, keyboard play of the very highest caliber, interesting and very effective guitar sound and styling choices, and some rather stupendous programming of the drums and rhythm section. This could've been early FROST* or BIG BIG TRAIN or THE FLOWER KINGS or THE TANGENT or even Open Sky-era IONA. I call this song a prog lover's wet dream! (15/15)6. "The Turk/Follow The Wind" (5:58) despite the relatively "weak" realistic tone and talent of singer Jake Livgren's voice, the music behind this song is, again, of the highest quality and caliber. Wow! Great chord and melodic pathways drive the music of this band deep into the pleasure zones of my brain. (9.5/10)7. "Nothing Is Everything" (7:34) more sophisticated and virtuosic symphonic prog music that features, this time, a real, "live" violin (though the previous one--on "The Plains? Truth" sounded just as authentic). The song moves through several motifs, shifting in keys and tempos while maintaining the piano-based full-spectrum prog with violin palette until the fourth minute in which Lisa's gorgeous piano play is isolated with guest Joe Deninzen's violin for a spell before the rest of the prog instruments rejoin. The melody choices are so awesome: piano and violin going back and forth each with totally-engaging lines and dynamics. At the five minute mark we move into a heavier, more dynamic section with pounding piano chords, guitar power chords, and soloing electric guitar before we bridge into a Spanish guitar-led section beneath which Lisa has the drums programmed with some excellent tom-and-bass drum flourishes. And soon enough it is over! Nice! I never expected that one to be an instrumental the whole way through. (13.75/15)8. "Carved From The Sun" (8:03) another stupendous prog rock instrumental that takes the listener on an exciting journey of dynamic multi-stimuli, all encapsulated into an action-packed whirlwind of enjoyable romantic slightly-pastoral NeoProg. Great bass, drum pacing, and, of course, keyboard work. I'm coming to fully comprehend what total melodic genius Lisa is: Amazing! So easy and comforting while never sacrificing sophistication and active lines from all of her instruments in the weaves. John's wah-wah-ed distorted guitar in the third minute is quite fitting but Lisa's continuous display of melodic and harmonic genius never quits! So many endorphin/goosebump moments generated by melodies, chord progression surprises, as well as palette and textural shifts. I am simply in awe. This is not only great prog it is music that I can (and will be) listen(ing) to for a long time into the future. This is music that not only rivals but I think surpasses that of my other favorite 21st Century NeoProg/Prog Folk band/artist, Solstice. (15/15)9. "Kicking Rocks" (4:20) though another great instrumental rendering (with a Marc COHN "Walking in Memphis"-like piano approach). Active bass, steady drums, organ and synths, and intermittent electric guitar shredding all add their sounds over the lively piano foundation. There is a weird "no sound" solo section at the end of the second minute but Lisa's confident piano playing never wavers, continues to deliver some wonderfully engaging work (to which I feel like playing "air piano"). The synth-supported multiple guitar soloing that occurs in the fourth minute is cool, too, but I could listen to Lisa's piano playing all day long--especially with recurring support of bursts of near-djenty bass-&-guitar passages. (9.125/10)10. "Prelude To Anywhere/Weekend Conquistadors" (5:45) more of the same piano styling from "Kicking Rocks" over and within which synths, shredding violins and metal guitars, as well as periodic bass and drums help out. There's a lot of the TRANS SIBERIAN ORCHESTRA Christmas music feel to this sound palette. John and/or Jake join in during a solo piano lull around the three-minute mark, signifying the switch to the "Weekend Conquistadors" half of the song--a lament about modern man's use (and misuse) of the land that once supported herds of bison and Native American tribes. Weird "distant and fading" strummed electric guitar ending as a couple quotes from literature or legend as delivered as spoken word over the top. (8.875/10)11. "Still Breathing" (5:58) long introduction eventually pans out in the second minute into a hard-driving violin-topped prog instrumental passage. This is disrupted around the 2:30 mark to allow plodding piano notes and increasingly thickening rock palette to support more of Lisa's computer-generated violin. John's guitars begin to increase in layers, gradually revealing some solo ideas until another sudden stop at the end of the fifth minute signals a shift back into the hard-driving motif of the second minute, over which John's twangy guitar steps up to really solo before the song's final chord--which is followed by a neighing horse whose hooves can then be heard galloping off onto the Plains. Solid prog if not so "perfect" as some of the previous compositions. (9/10)Total time 66:41There are many who will bemoan so much of this music being computer generated and "cleaned" but the end result--great prog music--cannot (and should not) be denied. Keyboard specialist Lisa LaRue is expressing a level of genius that not many prog artists have ever achieved. An album that is definitely in the running for 2026's Album of the Year--and deservedly so!A/five stars; a masterpiece of wonderful progressive rock music that taps into the palettes and energy of both the NeoProg and Prog Folk realms of progressive rock music and represent the talents of a musical genius who is totally new to me: Native American Lisa LaRue. HIGHLY recommended!

items.body: Belgian electronica pop act 808 Dot Pop has posted four videos since 14 August 2026, each pairing a track from an ongoing “-ism” naming series with a 20th-century building, ahead of two albums, “Minimalism” and “Maximalism,” due at the end of November 2026 via Alfa Matrix. The most recent, “Collectionism,” was posted on the artist’s official website on 17 September 2026. The four videos “Internationalism (Seagram)” was posted around 28 August 2026 and pairs the track with the Seagram Building in New York, an example of the International Style. The track itself is not available on the video’s own release: it appears exclusively on the various-artists compilation “Sounds From The Matrix 26” and will not be issued elsewhere. “Brutalism (Habitat 67)” followed on 6 September 2026, built around Moshe Safdie’s Habitat 67 in Montreal. The visual is as a digital reinterpretation of the building via “The Hillside Project” by NeoScape, rather than footage of the original structure. “Contextualism (Fallingwater)” was posted on 11 September 2026, pairing the track with Frank Lloyd Wright’s Fallingwater house. The version of “Contextualism” heard in this video appears on the “Minimalism” album, while a separate version of the same track, tied to the AT&T Long Lines Building, features on the lead single “Minimalism,” due 26 September 2026. “Collectionism” was posted on 17 September 2026. Unlike the previous three entries in this video 808 Dot Pop gives more info on a few upcoming fan packages. The ‘Minimalism’ and ‘Maximalism’ project 808 Dot Pop announced “Minimalism” (a white-sleeve album) and “Maximalism” (a black-sleeve album) on its website on 14 August 2026, describing them as “two completely different albums in content.” The lead single, “Minimalism,” is scheduled for 26 September 2026. Two further items are tied to the same releases. “Foundationalism,” a six-track EP featuring exclusive versions, is planned as a fan-shop exclusive on an NFC-equipped “phygital” card format. A 72-page fan book titled “Essentialism,” covering the architectural sites referenced across the campaign, was announced on 11 September 2026, with further details promised but not yet published as of this writing. A full tracklist and confirmed formats for “Minimalism” and “Maximalism” have not been published. About 808 Dot Pop 808 Dot Pop is the solo electronica pop project of Belgian musician Passenger S, also known for his work in Metroland. Side-Line reported his debut under the 808 Dot Pop name on 27 March 2020, in “Metroland’s Passenger S launches debut album under 808 DOT POP moniker”, ahead of the album “The Colour Temperature,” released on download and CD on 5 June 2020 on Alfa Matrix. Further singles followed the same year: “Incandescent,” the second single from “The Colour Temperature,” on 19 June 2020; a tribute cover of D.A.F.’s “El Que” for Alfa Matrix’s “Wir Sind DAF” compilation, released 2 October 2020; and “Kelvin (4200),” the third and final single from the debut album, on 13 November 2020, alongside a bundled triple 7-inch vinyl set covered by Side-Line in “Electro pop act 808 Dot Pop releases triple 7 inch vinyl singles in one bundle + 2 new download only singles” (6 November 2020). Side-Line also ran a ‘Click Interview’ with 808 Dot Pop in July 2020. The project continued with the “Ultraviolet” single campaign (February 2021) ahead of the album “The Cubic Temperature,” the “SunCatcher” EP (early March 2022) and a single dedicated to Guglielmo Marconi (January 2023), the latter featuring lyrics by Gary Hunter (Kraftman) and vocals by Lis Van Den Akker. Side-Line covered the act’s return with three simultaneous albums plus two EPs in “Belgian electronica act 808 Dot Pop back with 3 albums in one go + 2 singles” (27 March 2023) and a further double-EP release in “Electronica pop act 808 DOT POP returns with double EP” (5 June 2023). Most recently, fellow Alfa Matrix artist Cubic issued a rework album built on 808 Dot Pop material, covered by Side-Line in “Cubic drops 808 Dot Pop rework album ‘Back To 808’ on Alfa Matrix” (12 December 2025). The four-video architecture series and the wider “Minimalism”/”Maximalism” campaign mark the act’s first new album cycle since 2023.

items.body: UK synthpop and dark disco project KN/GHTS released the single “Light The Fuse” on 17 September 2026 via Specchio Uomo. The B-side carries a remix of “Supernatural Lover”, from KN/GHTS’s second studio album of the same name, by Berlin-based artist Daniel Knutz. Light The Fuse by KN/GHTS Specchio Uomo describes “Light The Fuse” as a pulsating and emotionally charged song about loss, recovery and finding yourself again. The track mixes synth pop, dark disco and italo disco elements with classic synth sounds. Daniel Knutz, whose own work draws on darkwave, coldwave, post-punk and minimal electronic, reworks “Supernatural Lover” as the release’s second track. An official video for “Light The Fuse” is out now, directed and edited by independent filmmaker Dirk Roche. It was filmed during the “Supernatural Lover Tour”, with additional footage from KN/GHTS’s live performances in Germany. About KN/GHTS KN/GHTS is the solo project of UK vocalist and songwriter James Knights, previously a singer of electronic pioneers Boytronic and known from his time in Scarlet Soho. Knights launched the project under the name Knight$, releasing the EPs “What’s Your Poison?” (2016) and “Alligator” (2017) before his debut album “Dollar$ & Cent$” came out on Cargo Records in 2019. Side-Line spoke to him about that album in a 2019 interview, in which he described the project as a faster-moving continuation of the sound he built with Scarlet Soho and Boytronic. The project later restyled its name as KN/GHTS and released its second studio album, “Supernatural Lover”, building an audience particularly in Germany, Sweden and Mexico. KN/GHTS combines synth pop, dark disco, electronic music and theatrical performance, and has performed live alongside Drab Majesty and Andy Bell of Erasure. “Light The Fuse”, released via Specchio Uomo, continues the project’s work following the “Supernatural Lover” album and tour.

items.body: Charlotte, North Carolina synthpop project Midniter, the solo vehicle of Nic Pugh, released the single and video “I Could Love You” on September 15, 2026, via Bandcamp and YouTube. It is the fourth and final promotional single ahead of Midniter’s debut album, “Xeno”, due October 27 on SugarTank! Records, the Charlotte label Pugh co-founded. The release coincides with the opening of vinyl LP pre-orders for “Xeno” through the label’s own store. Midniter describes “I Could Love You” as a ballad about unrequited love Pugh traced the song back to an unfinished piano piece: “‘I Could Love You’ came from an old piano tune that I never finished. The bookends of the song are directly from that idea, with the middle evolving into a more synthpop direction for Midniter. To me, it’s a pretty standard ballad about unrequited love – a tale as old as time that everyone can understand.” I Could Love You by Midniter The video for “I Could Love You” favors mood over narrative Pugh said the video leaves its meaning open: “The video is more ambiguous, playing with the question, ‘Is this about desire, obsession, or both?’ It’s ultimately your call to make. Our goal with this video was to focus more on mood than narrative. It was more important to live in these feelings of distance and longing than explain why they linger. The dancers, our friends from Baran Dance, were instrumental in carrying those moods throughout the video with their choreography. Our main actress Dustie Bayer was also incredible in her debut.” Paul Jahn of Yawn Productions filmed and edited the video, co-directing it with Pugh. Choreography comes from Baran Dance members Audrey Baran, Faith Centa and Donovan Granville, with Dustie Bayer in the lead acting role. For the silhouette performance scenes, Midniter expands to a trio with Joe Boyland and Dan Hitzelberger joining Pugh. Filming took place at Petra’s, the Charlotte venue where Pugh works and where Midniter’s 2025 debut single video, “Shoot the Moon”, was also shot, alongside a University of North Carolina dance studio and locations around Charlotte. About Midniter Midniter is the solo indie-electronic project of Charlotte, North Carolina musician Nic Pugh, launched in 2024 after roughly two decades in punk and rock’n’roll bands, including Paint Fumes and Jaggermouth. As Midniter, Pugh mixes synthpop songwriting with indie-electronic production, citing Radiohead, Justice, The Knife, LCD Soundsystem, Aphex Twin, Squarepusher and M83 as reference points alongside an “Indie Sleaze” visual style. Pugh co-founded Charlotte label SugarTank! Records with fellow musician Nic Holman; the label supports LGBTQ+ artists and allies. Midniter’s debut single, “Shoot the Moon”, arrived with a video shot at Petra’s in 2025, and Side-Line covered the project’s “Alarmist” video single that October. “I Could Love You” is the fourth and last of the promotional singles released ahead of Midniter’s debut album, “Xeno”, due October 27 on SugarTank! Records, with vinyl LP pre-orders now open through the label.

items.body: Town & Towers Records releases Eckotrigger‘s new single Imposter on Friday, September 18. The London and Copenhagen duo mixes synthpop, darkwave and alternative electronic songwriting on a track about confronting the past, emotional relapse and the search for inner peace. Eckotrigger describes “Imposter” as being “about trying to cut free from the past as we strive towards our own peace”. The song opens with the lines “I lay awake / In a sense of doom” before settling into a recurring refrain, “My emotional state / Takes me back to places”, that returns throughout the track to describe being pulled back into experiences the narrator believed had been left behind. The lyrics trace the process of letting go of people, memories and earlier versions of oneself, arriving at a closing message: “Nothing stays the same”. “Imposter” follows the release of Eckotrigger’s debut album “Reflections”, issued on CD and 12″ vinyl in late May 2026 and available through the band’s release page. The new single is not yet listed on the duo’s Bandcamp page; “Imposter” can currently be found through the Town & Towers Records aggregator link above, which routes to Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, Deezer, Tidal and SoundCloud. About Eckotrigger Eckotrigger is a duo formed in London, UK, comprising producer and instrumentalist Paul Dogra and vocalist and lyricist Joel Alexander. The pair, who now split their time between London and Copenhagen, built the project after playing in other bands and wanting to work without the friction of a full group, drawing on a shared appreciation for Depeche Mode, David Bowie, Nine Inch Nails, The Cure and The National. The duo released its debut single in December 2020 with an accompanying video addressing mental health and addiction, which received radio play and was discussed on BBC Radio. In September 2021, Eckotrigger performed in a 24-hour online concert for World Peace Day. The band signed to the Danish label Town & Towers Records in August 2022 and has since released several singles and an EP, including “Collide”, which appeared in its extended form on the conzoom Records compilation “electropop.25” in 2023. Joel Alexander has also lent vocals and lyrics outside the duo, featuring on Danish artist ee:man’s single “Slow Dream”, also released via Town & Towers Records. Eckotrigger played Elektroland Festival and Electrofest in Denmark in 2023, performed three UK concerts in 2024, supported Empathy Test, and played Emergenza Festival and the Live Wired event in Copenhagen in 2026. The band’s debut album, “Reflections”, followed on CD and 12″ vinyl in late May 2026. “Imposter” is the duo’s first single since that album.

items.body: Los Angeles club Das Bunker marks its 30th anniversary this October with three events: a Catch One show headlined by Combichrist on October 2, a Nine Inch Nails-themed boat cruise called Nine Inch Sails on October 10, and a Halloween dance party on October 31. Combichrist headlines Das Bunker’s 30th anniversary at Catch One Combichrist returns to Das Bunker for the first time since 2009 to headline the club’s official 30th anniversary show at Catch One on October 2. The set draws on the band’s first three albums, “The Joy of Gunz” (2003), “Everybody Hates You” (2005) and “What The Fuck Is Wrong With You People?” (2007). Richmond, Virginia’s The Treasury, whose sound mixes EBM, synth-punk, post-punk and 1990s techno, opens. Das Bunker resident DJs Mimi Cry, IHX, Franck H Bomb and The Operative play the rest of the 21+ night, which runs from 9pm to 3am. A Nine Inch Nails boat cruise and a Halloween party close out the month On October 10, Nine Inch Sails departs from Long Beach, California, the port city where Das Bunker started as a club. Das Bunker offshoot 90s Goth Klub and Depeche Boat present the 21+, three-hour, two-room cruise: DJ Bractune plays Nine Inch Nails on the outdoor deck while DJ Eser covers goth, darkwave and new wave on the second room. The anniversary month closes on October 31 with a Halloween party at Catch One, presented by 90s Goth Klub and Body Rhythm across two rooms of goth, darkwave and new wave. DJs J Bractune, Rev.John and Angel Tears play the 21+ event. About Das Bunker Das Bunker was founded in Long Beach, California on October 22, 1996, to spotlight industrial and related genres that other Los Angeles clubs overlooked before relocating its regular night to Catch One. Over three decades the club has hosted Front 242 and other established industrial and EBM acts alongside emerging names, and has run recurring nights including History of Industrial, Summer Massive and Das Bunker Star Wars Night. Its coverage has included the Los Angeles Times, Vice and Post Punk. Side-Line covered Das Bunker’s 29th anniversary last October, when Unter Null headlined at Catch One. This year’s 30th anniversary run adds Combichrist, a Nine Inch Nails cruise and a Halloween party to that annual tradition.

ルツェルン音楽祭が、セバスティアン・ノルドマン新総裁の企画である「序曲」と題した無料公演で、8月13日に開幕した。公開リハーサルの様相で、リッカルド・シャイー以下ルツェルン祝祭管弦楽団の楽団員は普段着だったが、それがまた親近感を抱かせる。 プログラムも、スティーヴ・ライヒ《ニューヨーク・カウンターポイント》のあとはガーシュウィン《キューバ序曲》、バーンスタイン《ウェスト・サイド・ストーリー》から〈マンボ〉と楽しめるプログラムだったのは、今年のテーマが「アメリカン・ドリーム」だからだ。シャイーはこのところ、これらのレパートリーを各地で披露しているといい、彼の新たな顔が見られる。 続いて会場のルツェルン・カルチャー・コングレスセンター（KKL）前に設置された野外ステージで、ハバナ・リセウム・オーケストラとベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団のホルン奏者、サラ・ウィリスがラテン調のモーツァルトや《カルメン》等、キューバ音楽を奏で、踊り出す聴衆も多くいて、熱いオープニングとなった。 15日は今年のアーティスト・エトワール、アウグスティン・ハーデリヒが登場、クラウス・マケラ指揮の祝祭管とバーバー「ヴァイオリン協奏曲」を研ぎ澄まされた音で奏で、まるでおとぎ話の世界のような共演だった。 2年前にアメリカの永住権も取ったというハーデリヒが愛情を込めて紡ぎ出す音に、マケラが応える様子が室内楽のように精緻だ。アンコールもアーヴィン・T・ラウズ《オレンジ・ブロッサム・スペシャル》で、アメリカンな選曲だった。 後半はストラヴィンスキー《火の鳥》を熱演し、マケラは何度も聴衆に呼び戻された。 8月17日はダニエル・バレンボイムが指揮するウェスト=イースタン・ディヴァン管弦楽団が、ヨーヨー・マとドヴォルジャーク「チェロ協奏曲」で匠の共演を聴かせた。後半はシューマン「交響曲第3番《ライン》」で若々しさも見せた。 8月23日にはコンポーザー・セミナーが6人の若手作曲家に委嘱した作品を、6曲一斉に世界初演した。このセミナーはピエール・ブーレーズが始めた現代曲アカデミーを基礎に、2016年にヴォルフガング・リームが立ち上げたもので、今年は4人の若手指揮者も招かれた。 作曲家同席の下、今年も110人が参加するルツェルン祝祭現代管弦楽団と創り上げた音が、歓びに満ちて生まれ出た。今年は日本人の参加者も多く、ヴァイオリンの伊勢宥奈、ヴィオラの布施海里、チェロの蕨野真美、フルートの矢島雄太郎、テューバの山本蒼太、ピアノの船橋佑花らが生き生きと演奏。日本の音楽界を支えていく次世代が、世界の現代音楽の第一線を学ぶ姿に頼もしさを感じた。 チェチーリア・バルトリの、涙を誘う《オルフェオとエウリディーチェ》 観客の拍手に応えるチェチーリア・バルトリ。今年還暦（60歳）を迎えた© Peter Fischli / Lucerne Festival 夜には当音楽祭の人気者、チェチーリア・バルトリがグルック《オルフェオとエウリディーチェ》で聴衆を喜ばせた。このプロダクションは、ザルツブルクからウィーンを回り、以前はチューリヒ・トーンハレでも見たが、その時よりも音楽的により深くなっていた。 暗くなった舞台にエウリディーチェ役のメリッサ・プティ（アモーレ役も兼任）が横たわり、蝋燭のような灯りを持ったモンテカルロ歌劇場合唱団が登場するだけで舞台装置ができあがる。そして彼らの歌により情景が描かれるため、字幕は必須、とバルトリは語る。 今年還暦を迎えた彼女はKKLを満たすほどの声量はないが、代わりに弱声はどんどん研ぎ澄まされ、涙を誘う。それに、ジャンルカ・カプアーノが指揮するピリオド楽器オーケストラ「モナコ公の音楽家たち」がそっと寄り添う。今回は歌詞を歌わずに叫ぶような部分も複数見られ、魂の震えを歌っていると実感させた。 有名なオルフェオのアリア〈エウリディーチェを失って〉は、いつもバルトリは超速で歌うのが残念なのだが、今回は繰り返し部分でしっとりと絶望感を表現したため、ここでも涙が込み上げる。 終演後、楽屋へ行くと、バルトリの御母堂も涙を溜めており、バルトリも「ほんとうに良い音楽」といって、まるでオルフェオとエウリディーチェの葬送に参列した人のようだった。この音楽的共感力が好演の理由だろう。
items._cn_summary: 本文为2026年卢塞恩音乐节开幕报道，涵盖多场演出实况。里卡尔多·夏伊指挥琉森节日管弦乐团演绎史蒂夫·赖希、格什温与伯恩斯坦作品，体现"美国梦"主题；克劳斯·马凯拉与哈德利希合作巴伯《小提琴协奏曲》后演出斯特拉文斯基《火鸟》；巴伦博伊姆携西东合集管弦乐团与马友友呈现德沃夏克《洛可可》。日本年轻音乐家在现代管弦乐团首演中表现活跃。巴尔托里以六旬之龄诠释格鲁克《奥尔菲斯与欧律狄刻》，弱声愈发精炼，配以古乐器乐团与蒙特卡洛合唱团，构成情感深沉的舞台。本文为新闻式报道而非深度乐评。

items.body: Lost Tribe Sound will be releasing three albums from William Ryan Fritch this summer. A History, in Boxes is a uniting between Fritch and writer and spoken word artist Matt Finney. The other two, an extended edition of The Old Believers and The Sum of its Parts, both come from his vault of music for film… A History, In Boxes is the sound of growing up, the sound of stepping onto the porch and arriving home after baseball practice. Youthful rites and rituals still burn in the heart: those endless, deep-pan summers still glint against the horizon, as do those first dates and the unashamed selfies that were taken as the sunset glowed against her face. Loving and losing both your teenage sweetheart and your virginity in encountering suffering for the first time is one part of the passage: the deep trauma of heartbreak is one of a thousand experiences that, while bittersweet, are there for a reason: they make you feel alive. Finney’s spoken word is from the heart, leaking with a delaying smile and a tear at the cusp of the eye, but it’s always full of appreciation and gratitude. This is a sweeping slice of Americana, a long-lost relation of a new, explosive folk with a soft inner centre (thanks to the banjo), with electro-acoustic elements similar in vein to post-post-rock. Wise and weary words say the things that’ve settled in the heart. Secret emotions come alive in these vocal love-letters, painting in cherry lipstick Finney’s sublime use of words. Sliding melodies and sun-drained strings swirl in the atmosphere, their light eclipsed by tall trees and summers gone. Propulsive drums energize the music, and they don’t want to give up the feeling – they cling to it. The drumming is elephantine in size and is also a primal war cry, a desperate appeal to anyone who’ll listen during the depths of heartbreak, while ‘Courthouse Wedding’ is a teenage dream, pre-drama, its bleached boards and high windows sunbathing in summer light. This album is about two women who changed my life. I loved them and lost them both. I was young and stupid and not ready for either of them but they taught me a lot. – Finney In 2014, only three years ago, William Ryan Fritch and Lost Tribe Sound began releasing a series of twelve albums over a two-year stretch. The Old Believers was a part of that gigantic Leave Me Series. Musically, The Old Believers has a very different tone. Its classical leaning automatically brings about a darker atmosphere. As well as bringing back the original score, the music has been rearranged and the album features eight new and reworked compositions. Music was used from two other recent films highlighting the harrowing situations of those displaced and seeking safe refuge, one of them being the 2016 academy award nominated documentary ‘4.1 Miles’. But calling the music a ‘score’ is a bit of an injustice. While it would be classified (urggggg) as soundtrack music, it’s so much more than that. Why should it prop up a scene on the screen when it has a life of its own? Soundtracks are usually staccato-stilted collections, but this is cohesive and broad in scope. Fritch’s compositions are jaw-dropping behemoths. His skills in this area are well-documented. Sure, we’ve known about them for a while, but that doesn’t diminish the power of the music. One segment emerges as a shy and softly-spoken soul, a delicately plucked instrumental, while the next explodes with volcanic force. The music has a common, brooding theme at its core, a tension that never settles or stabilizes; no resolutions, mirroring the horrors of uncertainty and the ill anxieties of a life without security or shelter. The strings don’t bend willingly towards a sense of peace. There are tender moments within, and their brevity makes it all the more moving. You can find temporary refuge in its crumbling stone walls and its ancient abbeys, and the album is long enough to find a secluded place within its music. ‘Who Fell the Last Tree’ adds to a sober sky, and its liberated percussion puts a thoughtful, mature musicianship in the limelight. There’s something of native tradition inside the music, of aged folk music and old ways. The dusty strings are caught up in an uneasy alliance with the present, a swirling integration that somehow works, but these old traditions give the music a feeling of warmth in spite of its overcast weather, and the music is kept safe from harm. The Sum of its Parts starts off in equally dark territory, thanks in part to its classical manifestations, its hanging notes and its low-registered appearances. You should never judge someone based on their appearance, though, and the same is true in music…if you look closer – deeper – you’ll find that the music is livelier than the leaden, conservative-leaning The Old Believers. The music’s got the blues, staring down into an empty bottle at two in the morning, but the second track seems to contradict this as strings wake up and smell the coffee. Come the morning, there’s no risk of a hangover. The swelling sun lights up the space in an orange and amber light, the glowing dawn promising something special for the day ahead. The music has a stronger aftertaste than coffee; when it begins to pump, getting into its proper gear, it carries something like the clanking of cogs in an iron machine, its smell like that of a copper coin or the frizzling air seconds before a lightning strike. The recurring motifs – a staple in film scoring – are strong enough to not need an accompanying image. The mood isn’t exactly oppressive, but its classical approach ages the music and wrinkles its skin…its bones appear as worn-down sets of ivory, but its spirit is spritely. The music gracefully transfers from a thoughtful mood to an energetic release, swooning into the unknown. Sometimes this happens in a single piece, as on ‘Subconsciously’, but others spread themselves out. So many artists overthink things…and their music asphyxiates because of it, burdened by unnecessary baggage and too much unrequited love – high on complexity and low on fun. Fritch’s earthy and colourful style knows no bounds; it’s illimitable. www.losttribesound.com
items._genre: folk / americana / spoken word / electro-acoustic / post-rock
items._cn_summary: William Ryan Fritch今年夏季将通过Lost Tribe Sound发行三张专辑。《A History, in Boxes》与口头诗人Matt Finney合作，以口语叙事串联成长记忆、失恋与仪式感，融合班卓琴、电声元素与滑动旋律，营造出美式民谣与后摇滚交织的怀旧氛围。Finney的旁白真诚且带有感激之情，音乐则提供推进感的鼓击与弦乐铺底。《The Old Believers》扩展版来源于其电影配乐档案，古典倾向带来更暗沉的色调，并加入八首新编作品，其中包括为2016年奥斯卡提名纪录片《4.1 Miles》所作的配乐。整体制作以电影配乐为基础，超越单纯画面支撑的功能，融入独立电影叙事与口述文学的元素。作为Lost Tribe Sound的小众独立发行，其跨界融合有一定的探索价值，但本质上仍偏向主流民谣与美式Americana范畴，与实验、前卫或电子等领域的契合度有限。

items.body: Bruno bavota has championed the piano since he first discovered its use as a musical instrument… Much of the record is populated by the dorian (bright) and mixolydian (mixed and misty) types of modes and keys. This type of playing – more whole tones than semitones (more white notes than black; less jazz notes and more classic). The corresponding metric structure of the pieces – adhering to traditional 4 and 8 bar phrases – keeps momentum. Meanwhile the tempo is a glacial coastal eddy over the waves, while with some sharper waves, always brings back to shore. It’s this light effect of all the techniques put together that creates an ennui that is long lasting and free flowing. The compositional clarion call is inclusive of strings as well, as on hugely emotive opener ‘Out Of The Blue’. The track sounds like a soundtrack to a non-sugary French or foreign film from somewhere long lost and idyllic. Comparisons can quite obviously be made to contemporary composers such as Nils Frahm and Eluvium, but there is something different here. Something out of the blue. Something forgotten. A posted note from the outlands of time. The reverse refrain aesthetic of the violins punctuating early sections of the album signify this perfectly. In the sense that instrumental levity is a beacon for change and formlessness, but solidity at the same time. One of those great paradoxes of the more that is put in, sometimes the more room for change amidst possible clutter. That is the most gorgeous thing amongst these misty tones, actually – the lack of clutter. The precision/rhythmicality. “Marea” is a slowly descending trip through G major down to E minor with a lovely sveltness to the strokes of the fingers. Additionally while pieces can be seen as quite short sometimes, the precision quality is heightened by their brevity. It is hard to pick any fault. The imagery conjured up is also bright, vivid contours of lush fauna; golden fields. Certainly not something doueur and depressing. Rather, one of those bolts from the blue. A gift from a blue skyline. www.brunobavota.com
items._cn_summary: Bruno Bavota 的这张专辑以钢琴为核心，结合弦乐与简约结构展开。整体风格偏向新世纪古典与氛围音乐的交界，使用多利安与混合利底亚调式营造明亮而朦胧的音色氛围。作品在传统四拍与八小节乐句框架内保持推进感，节奏舒缓如海岸暗流，偶尔泛起尖锐浪花后回归平静。小提琴的逆行式旋律动机与钢琴的精准触键形成对照，留白充分，避免了过度堆砌。从G大调缓慢下行至E小调的'Marea'展现出调性游走的细腻处理。乐评将其与 Nils Frahm 和 Eluvium 并置，强调其复古怀旧、带有失落异国电影配乐感的特质。整体创作手法克制而精致，但缺乏显著的实验性突破或跨类型融合，更接近氛围化的当代器乐作品。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由吉他手兼音乐档案学者Dominique Cravic与Les Primitifs du futur乐队合作，是该组合的第五张录音作品，由地下漫画家Robert Crumb绘制封面。专辑收录27首短曲，使用手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门琴、夏威夷吉他、风笛及音乐锯等多种乐器录制，融合了法国bal-musette、拉格泰姆、jug band、法国香颂及skiffle等多种风格。Cravic以近似Maurice Chevalier的口白式唱法演绎。曲目涵盖1925年老歌改编、抵抗运动歌手Juliette Gréco的致敬曲，以及对《Smoke Gets in Your Eyes》《Take Five》《As Time Goes By》等经典曲目的法语重新诠释。整张专辑体现了对被遗忘音乐风格的考古式复兴，以怀旧情怀和杂糅拼贴为主要特征。

items.body: Review by Grumpyprogfan — Quivira is the name of a road close to where I live. And with three reviewers hailing this a "masterpiece" and referencing the band Kansas - well, I had to check this out. The musicans are: Lisa LaRue, composer, keys, drum programming; John Baker, guitar, bass, vocals; Jake Livgreen, vocals; With... Joe Deninzon, violin, and Evan Stanley plays guitar on one song. The musicians are quite good and Lisa's compositions are good, but it has a Neal Morse / Flying Colors vibe more than a Kansas vibe, for me. I like that Quivira has lots of instrumental sections - where the musicians can jam - because the vocals are far from the majestic duo that was Steinhardt and Walsh. In fact, there aren't many vocals on this album at all. Overall, this is a good debut album, and if you enjoy a mostly instrumental retro 70's style of music, Quivira could be worth a listen. I'm curious is this a one-off, or is a second album with a human drummer a possibility? Solid 3.5 stars.
items._cn_summary: Quivira首张同名专辑由键盘手兼作曲家Lisa LaRue主导，融合了鼓机编程、吉他、小提琴与人声编制，整体呈现七十年代复古前摇滚风格。乐评人指出，作品更接近Neal Morse与Flying Colors的气质，而非Kansas那种华丽的双主唱合唱路线。专辑大量使用器乐段落，为乐手提供即兴jam的空间，人声部分相对克制。乐评认为这是一张品质尚可的出道作品，适合偏好器乐主导、怀旧色彩浓厚的前摇滚听众，但并未展现显著的实验性或跨界突破，在编曲与声响探索上趋于传统，旋律走向与和声结构偏向经典模式。

(Belgium). I was 14 years old...And the ladst one will be on October 20. 2026, in Madrid (Spain). Quite a long ride isn't it?This double CD starts with 2 killers: "Highway Star" & "Black Night".Difficult to imagine a better start! And the so afraid "karaokee" style is even forgotten during the latter. So far, so great!Two very good renditions of � tracks from "The Battle Rages On" (logical since it was released in 1993 (date of recording of this live set).then come a superb "Bethoven's Ninth"...the magic of Jon to combine classic with rock; A somptuous 10 minutes (or almost) track which brings me close to ectasy (at times!). To confirm the great shape, the great "Knocking on your Back Door" from "Perfect Strangers" adds to the general feeling. SUPERB!!!But, what to say write about the two pieces of resistance of this double CD set???"Child in Time" (from "In Rock") and the fabulous, and the best from all their live sets for "Anya".This closes CD1 that be rated as a 5* one.CD2 though will sound a little weaker.Not with "The Battle" nor "lazy" which are outstanding as well. But thereafter, the next 3 titels are shortered versions of known numbers just as on their "NEC" live. Press next. three tiems;Then, we are going to face an EXTRAordinary cover version of a mythical Stones song. My favorite of tyhis great rock band. "Paint it, Blcack". from hard rocking to spacey: it is soooo great. One of the too few highlights of disc 2.We're back on great track with "Speed King" (we can even hear some notes from "Burn" before minute 6 (only instrumental, 'cause Ian will NEVER sing sing it; nor any song from Mark 3.The last but one song is an OK version of "Hush" from Mark I...But the worse is goi,ng to happen to the overlooooong karaoke version of "Smoke on the Water".I really couldn't stand this while attending their concerts. What I did at the time, was going up to the floors and attend the bar to drink one (or two - remember, I'm Belgian) with one of my mates (hi, Jean-Pierre). It was in the Arena in Antwerp (just next door to the Sport Palace).The intro is fine (almost 3 minutes) is fine with me; As well as the core track...which leads us to minute 7.And then ...5 minutes of Smoooooooke on the Water...for about another 3 minutes.The audience might have loved this, but I didn't...Sorry guys...All in all, this is an excellent hard-rocking live album. Another one from Purple; THE MASTER, THE INVENTER of the genre.**** solid stars. .

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑收录了深紫乐队1993年的现场演出，曲目涵盖乐队各时期的代表作。开场以《Highway Star》和《Black Night》两首经典曲目快速点燃气氛，随后展现了乔恩·洛德将古典元素融入摇滚的手法，贝多芬第九交响曲的改编段落成为亮点。碟一整体水准较高，《Child in Time》和《Anya》被视作最佳演绎。碟二则显得稍弱，几首作品为短缩版编排，类似NEC现场的呈现方式。《Paint It Black》的翻唱从硬摇滚滑入太空感段落，是碟二中为数不多的亮点之一。《Smoke on the Water》的卡拉OK式延伸段落被批评为冗长拖沓。整体而言，这是一张硬摇滚风格扎实、但缺乏实验性突破的商业现场录音。

items.body: Kazayah sings “Sweet Love” over an instrumental that took its producers nearly three years to complete. That instrumental is Landmark Riddim, and it follows the Jamaican riddim format: a single backing track, with fifteen vocalists each recording a separate song to it. Stay Nice Music, the Maine label directed by Joshua “Don Daka” Smith, constructed it with co-producer David “Jah David” Goldmine, guitarist Lamont “Monty” Savory, Okiel McIntyre, I Grade‘s Laurent “Tippy I” Alfred and Spanish roots producer Roberto Sánchez, setting deep bass, clipped skank and warm horns beneath a one-drop the label terms One Drop Blues. Dub Shot Records issued the eighteen-track set on 21 August 2026, with Kumar Fyah recounting his detention over a small quantity of ganja, MediSun addressing freedom and Badda General on clash culture. Kazayah directs the rhythm towards a love song that reads a man’s arrival as ordained timing and measures the relationship by admiration, protection and the experience of being fully known. She was born Shanelle Mitchell to Jamaican parents in Evanston, on the northern edge of Chicago, sang in a Seventh-day Adventist congregation from childhood and reached roots reggae through a producer based in the same town. Her debut EP I Am Kazayah was released through Tuff Gong Worldwide, Ziggy Marley‘s label, and she has opened for him on tour. Hear “Sweet Love” on Landmark Riddim HERE The post Daily Discovery: Kazayah – Sweet Love appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 这张作品是典型的牙买加根源雷鬼合辑，Landmark Riddim 作为统一的器乐基底，邀请十五位歌手各自录制人声。制作方为美国缅因州独立厂牌 Stay Nice Music 与西班牙制作人 Roberto Sánchez 合作完成，发行由 Dub Shot Records 负责。Kazayah 是芝加哥出生的牙买加裔歌手，曾通过 Bob Marley 家族旗下 Tuff Gong Worldwide 发行 EP 并为 Ziggy Marley 巡演开场。Sweet Love 这首歌曲在传统一掉拍节奏上展开，以爱情为主题，描写关系中被完全了解与保护的感受。整体属于标准 riddim 格式的根源雷鬼制作，与实验、前卫、电子融合等方向距离较远。

items.body: Paulina Fae has released Lilac Cat, a six-song ethereal dream pop EP, on Projekt Records on 18 September 2026. The EP is out now digitally, streaming or pay-what-you-can on Bandcamp, and is also available on Spotify and YouTube Music. The six songs on ‘Lilac Cat’ The tracklist runs “Lilac Cat,” “Spinning Lullabies,” “In Veils of Spiderwebs,” “Aetheris,” “Wandermind” and “Noctivine.” Projekt Records describes the EP as a collection of “ethereal dream pop and otherworldly reverie,” moving from the “galaxy-eyed whimsy” of the title track and the “dream-jazz sounds” of “Spinning Lullabies” to the “faery-like currents” of “Aetheris,” with songs that wander through misty forests, celestial worlds and violet dreams carried by ethereal vocals. Lilac Cat by Paulina Fae ‘Lilac Cat’ follows Paulina Fae’s 2025 album “Ghostbirds,” a 10-song collection built around minimalist piano and soft, misty vocals, and continues her run of releases on Projekt Records, the label she has recorded for since 2012. About Paulina Fae Paulina Fae records under her given name, Paulina Cassidy, and has also used the name Polly Fae across her catalogue. Born in Ontario, Canada, she is a visual artist and songwriter based in Chattanooga, Tennessee, known for illustrated tarot and oracle decks including the Paulina Tarot, the Joie de Vivre Tarot, Witchlings, Pixiekins, Spiritsong Tarot and Phantasma Tarot, and for books such as “The Secret Language of Trees,” “Kindred Guardians” and “Mortimer: A Cat’s Journey in the Afterlife.” She self-released her earliest music as Paulina Cassidy through Ulaluma Productions, starting with “Bloodroots” in 2010, followed by “Time Traveler” in 2011 and “Lost in Oz” in 2012. She signed to Projekt Records the same year for the “Ice Iris” EP, followed by the album “Sugar Wingshiver” in 2014 and “Drawing up a Storm” in 2018. In 2019, recording as Polly Fae, she released the 15-track album “Dreamwalkers” on Projekt on 12 September, a limited-edition signed CD later followed by an instrumental version. The album “Phantom Gardens” followed the same year under the Paulina Cassidy name. Her Projekt output continued with “The Secret Language of Trees” and “Metamorphosis” in 2020, “Earthlight” in 2021 and “Glow” in 2022, alongside a “Dreamwalkers Instrumental” reissue. She contributed to the label’s “Purr24” various-artists compilation in 2024 and released the album “Ghostbirds” on 4 April 2025, followed later that year by a collaboration with Peter Phippen and Ivar Lunde Jr. on “The Phantom Moon.” “Lilac Cat” is her latest EP for Projekt Records, released 18 September 2026.

items.body: Top Pick?Game Over – Face the End (2025)No, that's not a mistake. Nothing's really doing it this week. Once upon a time, a Carly Rae Jepsen double-abum would be cause for celebration, but not in September of 2026. Similarly, while I seemed to enjoy 2016's For All Kings a lot more than most, and while the new Anthrax album isn't as bad as its AI Babadook magician-laden promo cycle suggested it might be, it's still far from recommendable. The need for some better thrash had me looking in the direction of Italian thrashers Game Over, but their new one—while perfectly fine— isn't really all that either. However, I remember referring to last year's Face the End in our Discord as "the best Anthrax album in years", but never ended up actually writing about it anywhere, so I'm choosing to give it a belated highlight here, in lieu of any better options.Going back to it now, my assessment of the album still stands. New vocalist Danny Schiavina gives hints of both John Bush and Joey Belladonna and the riffs are about as righteous as you can hope for from a longrunning re-thrash band these days. The quality of Game Over's records has always hovered "decent but not exciting", but I'd say Face the End sits only behind Crimes Against Reality (2016) in their discography and is well worth a listen if you overlooked it last year, or—like me—are just looking for a good thrash fix. items.body: Review by RojerWilco — If you're a fan of early Kaipa, you'll enjoy this set. Has it really been 40 years? Roine and Michael are as excellent as you would expect, and Tomas and Ingemar have apparently picked up right where they left off 40 years ago, literally not missing a beat. To me, the surprise is Lalle Larsson. As with his work in Karmakanic, he makes everything he touches better.The track selection has been picked from Inget Nytt Under Solen (Nothing New Under the Sun) and Solo, with Det Tysta Guldet (The Silent Gold) coming from the Kaipa daCapo album. Unless you're actively cross referencing their music, you wouldn't notice the new track among the classic ones.Consider this the missing link in the Kaipa discography. It is an excellent addition to any Kaipa collection, and also makes a good entry point for those interested in early Kaipa.

items.body: Young Medicine has signed a multi-album deal with FiXT, and the partnership opens with the re-release of “Immolator,” out now on the label. The Kansas City, Missouri trio pairs retro-styled synthesizers with hard rock and metalcore guitar work, and “Immolator” was first released in November 2025 through FiXT’s synthwave imprint FiXT Neon before returning now under the new deal. “Immolator” runs on thumping double-bass drums and crunchy guitar riffs under a chorus built from bright, retro synth lines, with the vocal shifting from a sung verse into screamed sections in the chorus and bridge. FiXT describes the track as “a high-energy collision of hard rock, metalcore, and alternative metal that pairs retro-inspired synthesizers with heavy guitars.” A visualizer for the song is streaming on YouTube. Immolator by Young Medicine “Immolator” is out now on all platforms through FiXT. About Young Medicine Young Medicine is a synth rock band from Kansas City, Missouri, made up of Bret Liber, Josh Hurst and Michael McEvoy. The band builds its sound around retro synthesizer tones layered with heavy guitars and hard rock and metalcore rhythm sections, mixing hooks from pop and rock songwriting with double-bass drumming and screamed vocal passages. Young Medicine first released “Immolator” in November 2025 through FiXT Neon, the synthwave-focused imprint of FiXT, the independent label founded in 2006 by Klayton of Celldweller. FiXT’s roster includes Celldweller, Scandroid, The Anix, The Browning and Rabbit Junk, among others, and its catalogue has been used in Westworld, Iron Man, Deadpool, John Wick and Call of Duty. The new multi-album deal makes Young Medicine a signed act on FiXT’s main roster, with “Immolator” as the first release under the agreement.
items._cn_summary: Young Medicine是一支来自密苏里州堪萨斯城的三人组合，以复古合成器音色搭配硬摇滚和金属核吉他为核心风格。专辑《Immolator》最初于2025年11月通过FiXT旗下的合成器浪潮子厂牌FiXT Neon发行，此次以多张专辑合约的形式在FiXT主厂牌重新发布。作品采用双底鼓与厚重吉他riff构建节奏骨架，副歌部分叠加明亮的复古合成器旋律线条，人声从演唱段落过渡到嘶吼段落。FiXT厂牌由Celldweller主创Klayton于2006年创立，旗下涵盖Celldweller、The Anix等以电子与重型音乐融合见长的艺人。该作品属于典型的合成器摇滚与金属核的拼贴式融合，旋律钩子偏向流行摇滚写作方式，合成器使用更接近复古合成器浪潮的表面化处理，缺乏深层声音设计或实验性结构探索，与暗潮、工业或电子音乐领域的真正融合存在明显距离。

items._cn_summary: 这是RootsWorld电台节目Race The Sky第027期的曲目列表，主持人Cliff Furnald精选了多组音乐人的作品。节目跨越民谣、根源音乐与独立创作领域，涵盖了Tom Waits、Eliza Carthy、Tom Russell等风格各异的艺人，既有美国西海岸的吟唱传统，也有英国民谣的传承。从节目编排来看，侧重于以人声为核心的创作型艺人，强调叙事性与地域色彩，航行至新泽西海岸再跨越大西洋，暗示节目对地理与文化背景的关注。整体定位偏向民谣与根源音乐的策展性推荐，涉及的世界音乐元素集中在英语语系传统内部。节目性质为电台播放列表，并非深度乐评，缺乏对音乐本身的分析性描述。

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由三位多伦多音乐人远程合作完成，历时多年通过邮件交流逐步累积，呈现出十八首短小精炼的微型作品，总时长仅三十四分钟。编曲以拨弦吉他、尤克里里、键盘和滑棒吉他为主，营造出类似梦境般飘渺的氛围。歌词主题围绕失去——失去爱情、失去自信，以及对世界荒诞的无奈接受。成员各自拥有不同背景，融合了民谣、电子流行、电视配乐等多种影响。制作风格在美国根源音乐框架内显得克制内敛，经济简练的编排配合清澈高亢的人声，试图以小巧体量传递温暖光芒。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets
items.label: Hudson
items._cn_summary: 这是一张围绕1819年英国彼得卢大屠杀历史事件创作的概念民谣专辑，由Young 'Uns成员Sean Cooney主导，集合了Eliza Carthy、Sam Carter等多位英国民谣歌手。专辑以原创歌曲形式重现集会当日的氛围——从期待与兴奋，到骑兵冲入人群的恐怖，再到事后的悲悼。歌词聚焦于Sam Bamford、Mary Fildes等普通人的故事，辅以同时代的信件、政治漫画和插图，呈现为一本多媒体书籍。乐评认为歌曲旋律有力，歌词意象精心选择，歌手演绎富有情感，在当下全球抗议受到压制的背景下具有现实意义。整体属于英国传统民谣与历史叙事民谣范畴，与实验、前卫、爵士、电子等方向距离较远。
